For derecognition the exception runs forward only: what Ind AS 109 asks on derecognition is applied prospectively, catching the transactions of the date of transition and the days after it, and nothing earlier than that. A non-derivative financial asset or liability derecognised under previous GAAP as the result of a transaction occurring before that date is therefore not recognised again under Ind AS, even where the Ind AS 109 criteria would not have been met — an NBFC that securitised a loan portfolio to a trust before transition, and derecognised it under Indian GAAP, does not bring it back on to the balance sheet. The items return only if a later transaction or event qualifies them for recognition. One door is left open: the entity may apply the derecognition requirements retrospectively from a date of the entity's choosing, but only where the information needed to apply Ind AS 109 to those past transactions was obtained at the time of initially accounting for them, not reconstructed afterwards.

citation.ref: Ch. Ind AS 101 First Time Adoption of Ind AS — mandatory exceptions, derecognition of financial assets and financial liabilities

concepts.section: Ind AS 101 First Time Adoption of Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 101 — Resetting cumulative translation differences at transition
concepts.statement: Ind AS 21 accumulates the exchange differences on translating a foreign operation in a separate component of equity and reclassifies them to profit or loss when the operation is disposed of, so a first-time adopter would in principle have to rebuild that accumulated balance for every foreign operation from the day each was acquired. Ind AS 101 offers an election out of it. If the exemption is used, the first-time adopter need not recognise those translation differences in other comprehensive income from the beginning and need not reclassify the pre-transition cumulative amounts on a later disposal, and the cumulative translation differences are deemed to be zero for all foreign operations at the date of transition. It is not available for one foreign operation and refused for another. The consequence carries to the far end: the gain or loss on a subsequent disposal of a foreign operation shall exclude the translation differences that arose before the date of transition and shall include only those arising after it.

citation.ref: Ch. Ind AS 101 First Time Adoption of Ind AS — optional exemptions, cumulative translation differences

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — what it is, and what happens when it and an Ind AS disagree
concepts.statement: A preparer sits below the Framework in one direction only: no Ind AS ever yields to it. The Framework carries none of the force of a Standard, cannot push aside anything an Ind AS requires, and is left out entirely when the standard-setter lists the pronounced set of Standards. Its first audience is the body that writes the Standards, so that each one is built from the same concepts as the last. A preparer gets two narrow doors into it — building a policy for a transaction no Ind AS covers, and choosing between options an Ind AS itself leaves open — plus a general use open to anyone, reading it alongside a Standard to understand what that Standard means. A Standard can still knowingly move away from a Framework idea: when the standard-setter judges that the reporting objective is better served by such a move, it makes that move on purpose and records why in that Ind AS's own Appendix. None of this hands a preparer a veto — where the wording of an Ind AS and the thinking in the Framework point in different directions, the Ind AS is what gets followed, and the Framework supplies no excuse for setting it aside.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: covers the Framework's standing beneath every Standard, its three roles for the standard-setter, for a preparer with no applicable Ind AS or a choice under one, and for readers generally, and the Appendix mechanism a Standard uses to record a deliberate move away from it

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — whom the statements are for, and the three things they cannot do
concepts.statement: Existing and potential investors, lenders and other creditors are who a general purpose financial report is built for, and its job is to give them information useful to a resource decision — an equity or debt purchase, sale or hold; a loan given or settled; or a vote cast, or influence exerted another way, over how management uses the entity's resources. Two things get read off the same information: where future net cash is likely to come from, and how well management has looked after the resources already entrusted to it, and the second is not a side benefit but part of what the reporting is for. Three things the reports were never going to manage. A user still needs to look elsewhere, at the wider economy, at politics, at how the industry is doing, because the report was never a complete picture on its own. Nor does it put a number on the entity itself — at most it gives users what they need to work one out themselves. And a regulator or a member of the public reading it does not become the audience it was written for; that audience is the resource providers named above, nobody else.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: covers the reporting objective and its three resource-decision classes, the pairing of future cash prospects with management's stewardship inside that objective, and the three named limits on what a general purpose report can do

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — relevance, and why materiality has no fixed percentage
concepts.statement: A user's decision changing because of a piece of information is what makes that information relevant, and it changes a decision through one of two routes, or both together. One route runs through prediction: nothing about this year's revenue analysis is a forecast, yet a user who feeds it into their own forward view has been helped by it, which is enough to call it predictive. The other route runs backward — the same figures often let a user check whether last year's predictions held up and adjust how those predictions get made, which is confirmatory value. Materiality then rides on top of relevance rather than beside it, as the form relevance takes for one particular entity. A fact is material where leaving it out, getting it wrong or burying it could plausibly bend what a primary user decides on the strength of that entity's own reports, and whether it clears that bar depends on how big or how significant the fact is, read against that specific entity's own circumstances. Nothing here supports a fixed percentage set in advance — an auditor's group-manual threshold might start a conversation, but the Framework's own test is never satisfied by importing one.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: covers the two routes to relevance, predictive and confirmatory, and materiality as relevance read for one entity's own facts rather than against any fixed percentage

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — faithful representation, and the word the Framework does not use
concepts.statement: Usefulness demands that a depiction match the substance of the thing it claims to show, not merely its outward form. When form and substance line up, describing the form settles the matter; when they pull apart, sticking to the form leaves the transaction misrepresented. Three marks together make a depiction fully faithful. It gives a user everything needed to follow the item, figure included — that is completeness. It carries no thumb on the scale in what gets picked or how it is put across, nothing tilted, inflated, played down or otherwise shaped to land well or badly with its reader — that is neutrality. And it is built without mistakes anywhere in the describing or in the choosing and running of the process behind the figure — that is being free from error, which is a different claim from being accurate. An unobservable value that has been estimated is neither accurate nor inaccurate in that sense; it still counts as faithful once it is flagged plainly as an estimate, its limits are spelled out, and the estimating process itself was picked and carried out cleanly. A later outcome landing somewhere else does not retroactively make that estimate wrong. One word is pointedly missing from all this: relevance and faithful representation are the Framework's two fundamental qualities, and reliability sits outside that pair. Ind AS 8 has not dropped the older word — when it guides a policy choice it still speaks of reliability, folding faithful representation into it as merely one of five strands alongside substance over form, neutrality, prudence and completeness.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: covers what makes a depiction faithful — matching substance over form, and the three marks of completeness, neutrality and freedom from error — set against Ind AS 8's older reliability language

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — prudence is caution, and it cuts both ways
concepts.statement: Prudence is what backs neutrality up, and the Framework gives that word a single job — caring under uncertainty when a judgement has to be made. That job is not conservatism, and it buys nobody a cushion. What often gets missed is that the rule cuts in two directions at once. One direction keeps assets and income from being puffed up and liabilities and expenses from being played down; the other, just as binding, forbids the opposite — running assets or income too low, or liabilities and expenses too high. A provision nudged past the best estimate on purpose, or an asset written down further than the evidence supports, is not prudent for having erred on the cautious side — it has simply failed the rule, and it has failed neutrality with it, since a picture skewed to look worse is exactly as biased as one skewed to look better. Prudence never made it onto the Framework's own list of qualitative characteristics in its own right; its role is to prop up neutrality, one of the three strands that make up faithful representation.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: covers prudence as caution under uncertainty supporting neutrality, and its two-directional bar against both overstating and understating assets, income, liabilities and expenses

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — the four enhancing characteristics and what they cannot rescue
concepts.statement: Four qualities — comparability, verifiability, timeliness, understandability — add polish to information that has already cleared the relevance and faithful-representation bar, and none of them, alone or combined, can rescue information that never cleared it. Consistency is the tool and comparability is what the tool is for: the same methods applied to the same items, this period against last and one entity against another, and none of that is uniformity, which would flatten genuine differences into false sameness. A depiction earns verifiability when separate observers, each informed and independent, would land on roughly the same view of it — directly, by checking an observed figure like a cash count, or indirectly, by rerunning a model's inputs through its own stated method and checking the output matches. Timeliness is nothing more than arriving while a decision can still be shaped by it, and while stale figures usually lose their edge, a trend can still make use of them. Understandability comes from clear classification, clear description and clear presentation, but complexity in the underlying facts is not a licence to cut them — doing that for the sake of an easier read would leave the report short and liable to mislead. None of this is written for the untrained: it assumes a user with a working grasp of business who reads with care, and even that user might reasonably bring in help. The four are worked through together rather than in a fixed order, and boosting one may mean giving up a little of another. A cost constraint sits over the whole exercise regardless — reporting something is only worth doing where its benefit to users is worth what it costs to produce and to use.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: covers the four enhancing characteristics as a ceiling on already-useful information, direct and indirect verification, and the cost constraint that sits over reporting decisions

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — a reporting entity need not be a legal entity
concepts.statement: Whether something counts as a reporting entity turns on whether it must, or elects to, put together financial statements — nothing more, so a single company, a slice of one, or a group of several can each qualify, and legal-entity status is beside the point. A parent bundled with its subsidiaries produces consolidated statements; the parent taken on its own produces separate or standalone ones; several entities joined without every one of them sitting under a common parent produce combined statements. Legal form will not always mark out where the entity's edge falls, and where it does not, that edge gets drawn instead from what the primary users need to know, subject to three faithful-representation checks — the economic activities swept inside cannot be picked arbitrarily or left incomplete, whatever is swept in has to yield a neutral picture, and the statements themselves must spell out how that edge was drawn and what sits within it. A subsidiary's own affairs are not what consolidated statements exist to report on — that job belongs to the subsidiary's own statements. And a parent's unconsolidated statements, useful as they might be to that parent's own creditors, generally fall short of what those creditors need, so they cannot stand in wherever consolidated statements are called for.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: covers what qualifies as a reporting entity regardless of legal form, the three kinds of statement that follow, the faithful-representation checks on a boundary not set by legal form, and why unconsolidated statements cannot substitute for consolidated ones

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — an asset is a present right, not an expected inflow
concepts.statement: Three things have to be true together before a right becomes an asset: the entity controls it now, past events put it there, and it carries potential to pay off economically — an economic resource, in the Framework's own shorthand, being exactly that kind of right. It is the middle test, potential, where the newer wording pulls away from the old. Nothing about certainty or even likelihood is asked for here — a right clears this bar so long as it already exists and at least one scenario would see it pay off for this entity in a way outsiders do not share. A right with only a slim chance of paying off is therefore still an asset on this test; that slim chance only starts to matter later, when the questions become whether to recognise it and at what figure. Ind AS 38 sets a stiffer bar than this — a resource has to be one future benefits are expected from, with a probability test layered on before recognition follows. Two more things trip people up. What the entity holds is the right itself, not whatever the right might someday yield — a purchased option's resource is the right to exercise it, never the cash the exercise might later bring in. And spending money is evidence of chasing a benefit, never proof one was landed, just as spending nothing proves nothing either way — a right handed over free by a government, or simply gifted, is exactly as much an asset as one that was bought.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: covers the three-part asset test of control, past event and potential, why the potential test does not need certainty or likelihood, the resource-versus-benefit distinction, and the weaker probability standard here against Ind AS 38's stricter one

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — control, the agent, and the right an entity cannot hold against itself
concepts.statement: Deciding which entity a resource belongs to, for accounting purposes, is exactly what the control test does — an entity holding a proportionate share of a property books that share alone, never the rights attaching to the whole thing. Two things together make the test: being able right now to steer where the resource is put to use, whether by using it directly or letting somebody else use it, and being able to capture whatever economic benefit that use generates. Built into that is the power to keep everyone else out, which is also why a resource cannot answer to two masters — once one party has it, nobody else does. Enforceable legal rights usually carry control, though they are not required for it; secret know-how can be controlled through nothing more than access plus the ability to keep it from spreading, with no patent anywhere near it. A resource whose payoff swings sharply for one party can point toward that party controlling it, but that swing is only ever one input into a broader judgement, not a test on its own. Two edge cases matter. An agent holding something on a principal's behalf never turns that something into the agent's own asset, and passing it on to a third party is likewise never the agent's own liability — the resource being moved was always the principal's. And self-dealing produces nothing: an entity cannot owe itself a benefit, so shares it buys back and holds are not its resource, and the same goes for one group company's instrument sitting in another group company's hands.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: covers the two-part control test of directing use and capturing benefit, why control cannot sit with two parties at once, the principal-and-agent treatment, and why self-held or intragroup instruments are not economic resources

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — a liability turns on what the entity cannot practically avoid
concepts.statement: Three tests together turn a duty into a liability, all needed at once: a present obligation, to move an economic resource out of the entity, and that obligation has to trace back to something that already happened. Owing somebody is the core of an obligation — a duty the entity has no real way of sidestepping, owed to a party who need not even be named yet. Plenty of obligations start in a contract or a statute; others grow out of the entity's own habits, its published commitments or specific promises it has made, wherever backing away from them is not a real option — those are the constructive ones. Where moving the resource only happens if the entity first takes some step of its own choosing, an obligation only exists if stepping back from that step is not realistically available — which is exactly why choosing the going-concern basis for the accounts carries its own hidden conclusion: that the entity has no real way of dodging a transfer it could only dodge by winding up or shutting down trading. Merely meaning to make a transfer, or it being highly likely, settles nothing by itself. The transfer test itself sets a low bar deliberately: it never needs to be certain, or even probable, that a transfer will be needed — one single scenario where the obligation would call for it is plenty, so a low-odds obligation still qualifies. It is the past-event test that does the real work. A present obligation only exists once the entity has already taken the benefit, or already acted, in a way that leaves it facing a transfer it would otherwise never have owed. None of this cares when payment falls due — a debt payable next year is a liability today.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: covers the three-part liability test, constructive obligations arising from an entity's own conduct, the going-concern basis read as an obligation an entity cannot practically escape, and why the past-event test is the strict one of the three

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — choosing the thing the criteria are applied to
concepts.statement: Recognition criteria and measurement concepts never land on raw facts directly — they land on whatever slice gets chosen as the unit of account, which can be one right, a bundle of rights, one obligation, a bundle of obligations, or a mix of both. That slice gets picked with one goal: making the resulting numbers, both the item itself and the income or expense it throws off, relevant and a faithful match for what actually happened. Nothing forces the same slice to be used twice over — recognition can happen contract by contract while measurement happens portfolio-wide, and presentation can later regroup or split what recognition and measurement already settled. Strictly, every separate right is its own asset, yet related rights typically get folded into one: land brings with it the right to use it, to sell rights attached to it, to pledge it and more, and treating that whole bundle as a single asset is usually the tidiest faithful account of it. Rights and obligations born from the same source and impossible to prise apart form one inseparable unit; where they can be prised apart, separating them may be the better call. A set of contracts built to achieve one overall commercial outcome can likewise force itself into a single unit — two contracts signed at once with the same party that cancel each other out create, between them, nothing at all. Equally, one contract bundling rights that could have sat in two separate contracts may need to be unpicked and accounted for that way. Offsetting is a wholly different move and is rarely the right one — it takes two units of account, an asset and a liability, that were kept separate, and nets them into one balance-sheet figure, which lumps unlike things together.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: covers what a unit of account is and why recognition and measurement need not share one, related rights bundled into a single asset, inseparable rights and obligations, contracts read for their combined commercial effect, and why offsetting is a different operation

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — the contract neither side has performed
concepts.statement: Neither side having moved yet, or both sides having moved by the same amount, is what makes a contract — or part of one — executory. What it creates is one combined right-and-obligation pair to swap economic resources, and since the two halves cannot be pulled apart, the whole thing books as a single asset or a single liability, never a right sitting on one side and an obligation on the other. Present-day terms decide which of the two it is: favourable terms today make it an asset, unfavourable terms today make it a liability, and a shift in prices can flip it from one to the other. Getting that classification right says nothing yet about whether the figure actually shows up in the statements — that is a separate question answered by the recognition criteria and by whichever measurement basis applies, onerous-contract testing included. Performance by either side chips away at the executory status. Take an employment contract: no obligation to pay wages exists yet, because up to the point work is done, all the entity is holding is a combined right to future service paired with an obligation to pay once that service arrives.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: covers what makes a contract executory, why it books as one combined asset or liability, how current terms decide which, and how performance narrows what remains executory

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — meeting a definition is necessary and not sufficient
concepts.statement: Capturing something in the balance sheet or in profit and loss, at a figure called its carrying amount, is what recognition means, and the gate to get there has two steps rather than one: meeting an element's definition is necessary but never by itself sufficient. Recognition only follows where doing so gives statement users something useful — relevant, and a faithful picture of the item together with whatever income, expense or equity change it generates. Relevance can be undermined in two ways, neither one automatic and neither decisive on its own — genuine doubt about whether the asset or liability even exists, or its existing but with only a slim chance of any inflow or outflow. Faithful representation can be undermined where measuring the thing is so uncertain that no measure on offer would help anybody — an outcome range that is unusually wide, a figure unusually sensitive to small shifts in probability, or a cash-flow allocation that is unusually subjective — and only in that narrow band does the item stay off the statements. Being kept off is not the end of the story: the notes may still need to carry enough about it to make up for its absence from the balance sheet. Two absences in the Framework deserve naming directly. Neither a probability cut-off nor a stand-alone reliable-measurement test appears anywhere in it, which is exactly why Ind AS 38's own test — benefits expected plus cost reliably measured — sets a narrower gate than the Framework does. And matching costs against income was never one of the Framework's aims; income and its related expense showing up together falls out of what the balance sheet already holds, and none of that licenses parking something in the balance sheet that fails every element definition.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: covers the two-step recognition gate, how existence doubt or low inflow probability can defeat relevance without doing so automatically, when measurement uncertainty keeps an item off the statements, and why matching is not a Framework objective

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — taking it off, and what is left behind
concepts.statement: Taking an asset or liability off the balance sheet, wholly or in part, is derecognition, and it is normally triggered by the same thing that got it recognised in the first place ceasing to hold — control slipping away for an asset, a present obligation ending for a liability. Three steps carry it out. Whatever part expired, was used up, was collected, was settled or was handed over gets taken off, with the resulting income or expense booked. Whatever part is kept carries on being recognised, now standing as its own separate unit of account from the part that left — and being separate means nothing gets booked against it just because its former partner is gone, unless the event itself changes what measurement basis now applies to it, which is exactly what happens when a parent loses control of a subsidiary and has to remeasure the stake it keeps at fair value. From there, the retained part gets shown on its own, the income and expense tied to the departed part get shown on their own, and the whole thing gets explained. One trap: looking like a transfer is not the same as being one. Keep enough exposure to how an asset's benefits might swing, up or down, after supposedly handing it over, and that exposure can point to control never having actually left; hand the asset to someone acting merely as agent, and control stays with the transferor regardless of who is now holding it.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: covers derecognition as removal triggered by losing the defining feature, the three-step treatment of the transferred and retained components, and when an apparent transfer is not a real one

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — historical cost against the three current values, and how one is chosen
concepts.statement: Pick a feature of the item to be measured, and applying it as the basis produces a figure for the item itself and for whatever income or expense follows from it. Four bases exist, and one sits apart from the other three. Historical cost starts from the original transaction price and only ever moves for things like consumption, collection, settlement, impairment, an onerous turn, or interest building up on a financing element — value changes in the market pass it by entirely. The other three all reset to conditions on the measurement date itself. Fair value asks what an orderly market transaction between willing participants would fetch on selling an asset or would cost to transfer a liability — an outsider's exit price, arrived at before any deduction for disposal costs and with acquisition costs left out of it altogether. Value in use (for an asset) and fulfilment value (for a liability) instead discount the entity's own expected cash flows — from using and eventually disposing of the asset, or from meeting the liability — built on assumptions specific to this entity, not visible in any market, worked out with cash-flow modelling, excluding costs incurred on first recognition but folding in the present value of whatever it will cost to dispose of or settle later. Current cost behaves like historical cost in kind — an entry value built from consideration plus transaction costs — but it gets reset at every measurement date instead of being locked in at acquisition. None of the four wins by default; the choice is judgement suited to the item. Assets like plant or inventory, which generate cash only indirectly through being used together with other things, usually call for historical or current cost; an asset that can be sold on its own without real penalty and generates cash directly usually calls for a current value instead. Splitting an asset and a liability whose cash flows move together across two different bases creates a mismatch that can undercut faithful representation, which is exactly why Ind AS deliberately mixes bases rather than running on fair value throughout — mixed is not the same as inconsistent.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: covers the four measurement bases and the entry-value/exit-value split among them, the perspective and cost treatment each reflects, and the factors that decide which basis fits an item and avoid a mismatch between linked ones

concepts.section: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Conceptual Framework — the two concepts of capital, and the profit each one leaves
concepts.statement: What users of an entity's statements actually care about decides which concept of capital gets used. Users focused on the money invested holding its nominal amount or its purchasing power point the entity toward the financial concept, where capital means net assets or equity; users focused on the entity's ability to keep operating point it toward the physical concept, where capital means productive capacity. This is not a labelling exercise — whichever concept is chosen becomes the yardstick profit is measured against, since profit only exists to the extent capital at the close of the period beats capital at its start, once anything paid to or put in by owners is stripped out. The financial concept treats a period as profitable only when the money value of net assets is higher at the end than it was at the start, and that money value can be tracked either in nominal monetary units or in units of constant purchasing power. The physical concept instead treats a period as profitable only when productive capacity itself has grown. Where the two concepts really pull apart is in how each treats a change in the price of the entity's own assets and liabilities, and one set of facts run through all three readings gives three different answers. Read in nominal monetary units, a gain simply from holding an asset through a price rise counts as profit in principle, even if it only gets booked once the asset is actually sold. Read in units of constant purchasing power, only the slice of that price rise beyond general inflation counts as profit, and the remainder sits in equity as a capital maintenance adjustment instead. Read under the physical concept, every one of those price changes is treated purely as a shift in how much productive capacity is now on the books, so none of it is profit — all of it lands in equity as a capital maintenance adjustment.

citation.source: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Ind AS
citation.ref: covers the financial and physical concepts of capital, what fixes the reference point for profit under each, and how the same price change is read three different ways under nominal monetary units, constant purchasing power, and the physical concept

concepts.section: Ind AS 115 Revenue from Contracts with Customers
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 115 — Revenue from Contracts with Customers
concepts.statement: Revenue is recognised when (or as) a performance obligation is satisfied by transferring control of the promised good or service to the customer. Transfer of control, not transfer of risks and rewards, is the recognition trigger.

citation.ref: para 31

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 2 — Inventories
concepts.statement: Inventories of items that are not ordinarily interchangeable are costed by specific identification. For the rest, FIFO or weighted average is used. LIFO is not permitted.

citation.ref: para 23 to 25

concepts.section: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 110 — Consolidated Financial Statements
concepts.statement: An investor controls an investee only when it has all three elements together — power over the investee, exposure or rights to variable returns, and the ability to use its power to affect those returns. Control does not require a majority shareholding.

citation.ref: para 7

concepts.section: Accounting and Reporting of Financial Instruments
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 109 — Financial Instruments
concepts.statement: Loss allowances are measured on an expected credit loss basis, recognised from initial recognition without waiting for a default. For trade receivables the simplified approach applies, and the allowance is always lifetime expected credit losses.

citation.ref: para 5.5.15

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 103 — Business Combinations
concepts.statement: Under the Indian carve-out, a gain on a bargain purchase is recognised in other comprehensive income and accumulated in capital reserve, not in profit or loss — unlike IFRS 3, which takes it to profit or loss.

citation.ref: para 34 and 36

concepts.section: Ind AS 115 Revenue from Contracts with Customers
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 115 — Revenue from Contracts with Customers
concepts.statement: A performance obligation is satisfied over time only when one of three criteria is met — the customer consumes the benefit as the entity performs, the customer controls the asset as it is created, or the asset has no alternative use and the entity has an enforceable right to payment for performance to date. Otherwise control passes at a point in time.

citation.ref: para 35

concepts.section: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 37 — Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets
concepts.statement: A provision is recognised only when all three conditions hold — a present obligation, legal or constructive, from a past event; a probable outflow of resources; and a reliable estimate. For a restructuring, the obligating event is announcing the plan to those affected or beginning to implement it, never the board decision alone.

citation.ref: para 14 and 72

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 16 — Property, Plant and Equipment
concepts.statement: The cost of a major inspection or overhaul that is a condition of continuing to operate an asset is capitalised into the asset's carrying amount when incurred, and any remaining carrying amount of the previous inspection is derecognised — even if the previous inspection's cost was never separately identified.

citation.ref: para 13 and 14

concepts.section: Ind AS on Items impacting the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 21 — The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates
concepts.statement: At each reporting date, foreign currency monetary items are translated at the closing rate, with exchange differences to profit or loss. Non-monetary items carried at historical cost stay at the transaction-date rate. Whether an item is money fixes which rate it gets.

citation.ref: para 23

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 38 — Intangible Assets
concepts.statement: Internally generated goodwill is never recognised as an asset, and internally generated brands, mastheads, customer lists and similar items are barred with it. Development costs are the exception, capitalised only from the day all six conditions are demonstrated; research is always expensed.

citation.ref: para 48, 54 and 63

concepts.section: Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 108 — Operating Segments
concepts.statement: An operating segment is separately reportable if it crosses ten per cent of combined revenue (internal plus external), of the greater of combined profits or combined losses, or of combined assets — and reportable segments must together cover seventy-five per cent of external revenue, adding segments until they do.

citation.ref: para 13 and 15

concepts.section: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 1 — Presentation of Financial Statements
concepts.statement: A liability sits outside current liabilities only where, on the reporting date itself, the entity holds a right to put settlement off for twelve months or more and that right is real rather than nominal; the amended standard dropped the older demand that the right be unconditional. Covenants the entity has to meet by the year end shape the classification, later ones do not. Where such a covenant is broken and the money becomes callable, which answer is right turns on when the year began. For a year beginning on or after 1 April 2025 and ending before 1 April 2026, India kept a relief: the loan stays non-current if the lender backs off between the year end and the day the accounts are approved. For a year beginning on or after 1 April 2026 that relief is withdrawn, so the loan is current however kindly the lender behaves afterwards. Under both, a grace period the lender granted by the year end and running more than twelve months past it keeps the loan non-current.

citation.ref: para 74 and 75

concepts.section: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 7 — Statement of Cash Flows
concepts.statement: Under the Indian carve-out, an entity other than a financial institution classifies interest paid as a financing cash flow and interest and dividends received as investing — the options IFRS offers are removed. A bank classifies all of them as operating, because lending is its business.

citation.ref: para 33

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 116 — Leases
concepts.statement: A lessee recognises a right-of-use asset and a lease liability for every lease, with two elections out — leases of twelve months or less with no purchase option, and leases of low-value assets. The exemptions are elections about recognition, not about whether the contract is a lease.

citation.ref: para 5 and 6

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 36 — Impairment of Assets
concepts.statement: Recoverable amount is the larger of two measures — value in use, and fair value net of the costs of disposing of the asset. A write-down bites only where the carrying figure stands above that larger measure, so an entity that can either sell well or use well takes no impairment: one route alone is enough to clear the asset.

citation.ref: para 6

concepts.section: Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 10 — Events after the Reporting Period
concepts.statement: An event after the reporting period adjusts the financial statements only when it evidences a condition that existed at the reporting date; a condition that arose afterwards is disclosed, not adjusted. Dividends declared after the reporting period are the standard's own worked example — no liability at the reporting date, however certain the declaration.

citation.ref: para 3 and 12

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 105 — Non-current Assets Held for Sale
concepts.statement: Held-for-sale classification needs the asset available for immediate sale in its present condition and the sale highly probable — management committed to a plan, an active programme to find a buyer, active marketing at a reasonable price, and completion expected within a year. Once classified, depreciation stops and the asset sits at whichever is lower — its fair value less costs to sell, or the carrying amount it came in with.

citation.ref: para 6-8

concepts.section: Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 8 — Policies, Estimates and Errors
concepts.statement: A change in accounting policy is applied retrospectively, restating comparatives as if the new policy had always applied; a change in accounting estimate is recognised prospectively, in the period of change and the future. Where the two are hard to tell apart, the standard itself says treat the change as an estimate. Depreciation method and useful life are estimates; measurement basis is policy.

citation.ref: para 19 and 36

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 23 — Borrowing Costs
concepts.statement: Borrowing costs directly attributable to acquiring, constructing or producing a qualifying asset — one that necessarily takes a substantial period to get ready for its intended use or sale — are capitalised as part of the asset's cost; all other borrowing costs are expensed. Capitalisation is suspended during extended periods when active development pauses, and ends when the asset is substantially ready.

citation.ref: para 8

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 40 — Investment Property
concepts.statement: Ind AS 40 permits only the cost model for investment property — the Indian carve-out removed IAS 40's fair value model. Fair value is still measured and disclosed in the notes, but the balance sheet carries cost less depreciation and impairment. Property held to earn rentals or for capital appreciation, not for use in production or administration, is what the standard covers.

citation.ref: measurement after recognition (cost model; fair value model not permitted)

concepts.section: Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 113 — Fair Value Measurement
concepts.statement: The fair value hierarchy ranks inputs, not techniques: Level 1 is unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical items; Level 2 is other observable inputs — quoted prices for similar items, or corroborated market data; Level 3 is unobservable inputs. A measurement sits at the lowest level of any input significant to it, and Level 1 prices are used unadjusted where available.

citation.ref: para 76, 81 and 86

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 102 — Share-based Payment
concepts.statement: For equity-settled awards to employees, the expense is measured at the fair value of the equity instruments at grant date — and that value is never remeasured, however the share price moves. What does move is the number of awards expected to vest under service and non-market conditions, trued up each period until vesting. Market conditions are priced into grant-date value once and never trued up.

citation.ref: para 10-11

concepts.section: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 19 — Employee Benefits
concepts.statement: Defined benefit cost splits three ways: service cost and net interest go to profit or loss; remeasurements — actuarial gains and losses, and the return on plan assets beyond the amount already in net interest — go to other comprehensive income, and once there they are never reclassified to profit or loss. The split keeps the operating result clear of actuarial volatility without hiding it.

citation.ref: para 120 and 122

concepts.section: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 28 — Investments in Associates
concepts.statement: Twenty per cent or more of voting power presumes significant influence — the power to participate in financial and operating policy decisions — and less than twenty presumes its absence; both presumptions yield to clear demonstration otherwise. Board representation, policy participation, material transactions, interchange of personnel or essential technical dependence can evidence influence below the line. An associate is equity accounted, not consolidated.

citation.ref: para 5-6

concepts.section: Ind AS on Items impacting the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 12 — Income Taxes
concepts.statement: A deferred tax asset on unused tax losses is recognised only to the extent future taxable profit is probable — and a history of recent losses is itself evidence against that. A loss-making entity records the asset only to the extent of taxable temporary differences or convincing other evidence of future profit, such as a firm order book from a cause that has demonstrably ended.

citation.ref: para 34-35

concepts.section: Accounting and Reporting of Financial Instruments
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 109 — Classification of financial assets
concepts.statement: A financial asset is carried at amortised cost only when both tests pass: the business model is to hold and collect contractual cash flows, and those cash flows are solely payments of principal and interest. Held-to-collect with equity-linked returns fails the second; plain-interest bonds bought for trading fail the first. Failures land in fair value categories.

citation.ref: para 4.1.2

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 103 — Non-controlling interest at acquisition
concepts.statement: For each business combination, the acquirer measures qualifying non-controlling interest at either full fair value or the proportionate share of the acquiree's identifiable net assets — a choice made combination by combination, not as a standing policy. The choice sets goodwill: fair value NCI produces full goodwill including the minority's share; the proportionate route recognises only the acquirer's goodwill.

citation.ref: para 19

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 116 — Lessor accounting
concepts.statement: Lessors still classify: a lease that transfers substantially all the risks and rewards of ownership is a finance lease — derecognise the asset, recognise a receivable; otherwise it is an operating lease — keep the asset, book income over the term. Indicators include ownership transfer, a bargain purchase option, the term covering the major part of economic life, and present value of payments amounting to substantially all the fair value. Lessee accounting became single-model; lessor accounting did not.

citation.ref: lessor classification (finance vs operating)

concepts.section: Accounting and Reporting of Financial Instruments
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 32 — Liability or equity
concepts.statement: An instrument is classified by substance against the definitions, not by its legal name: a contractual obligation to deliver cash — mandatory redemption, compulsory dividends — makes a financial liability, however the instrument is titled. Preference shares redeemable at the holder's option or on a fixed date are debt; pure discretion over both dividends and redemption keeps an instrument in equity. Classification happens once, at issue.

citation.ref: para 11 and 15

concepts.section: Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 33 — EPS and bonus issues
concepts.statement: A bonus issue, split or similar event changes the share count without changing resources, so EPS treats the new count as if it had existed from the beginning of the earliest period presented — restating the comparative EPS too. A fresh issue for cash, by contrast, enters the weighted average only from its date, because new resources arrived then.

citation.ref: para 27-28

concepts.section: Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 24 — Related Party Disclosures
concepts.statement: Key management personnel compensation is disclosed in total and by category — short-term, post-employment, other long-term, termination, share-based. Related party disclosure is about relationships and transactions, not approval: arm's length terms may be claimed only if they can be substantiated, and a government-related entity gets a partial exemption for dealings with its government and its sister entities, disclosing the nature and extent instead of every transaction.

citation.ref: para 17

concepts.section: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 34 — Interim Financial Reporting
concepts.statement: Interim statements apply the same accounting policies as the annual ones — a quarter is not a licence for different measurement — and reporting frequency must not change the annual result: measurements run year-to-date, so a third-quarter estimate correction adjusts the year-to-date figures rather than fabricating a standalone quarter. Costs that fail asset definitions at year-end fail them equally at a quarter's end.

citation.ref: para 28

concepts.section: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 37 — Onerous contracts
concepts.statement: A contract whose unavoidable costs of fulfilment exceed the benefits expected under it is onerous, and the present obligation is provided for at once — the unavoidable cost being the lower of the cost of fulfilling and the penalty of exiting. Routine cancellable purchase orders create no obligation, and expected future operating losses of the business generally are never provided for; the onerous contract is the exception because the loss is contracted, not merely forecast.

citation.ref: para 66-68

concepts.section: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 111 — Joint operations and joint ventures
concepts.statement: Joint control is contractually agreed sharing of control where the relevant decisions need unanimous consent. The arrangement's type decides the accounting: joint operators have rights to the assets and obligations for the liabilities and record their share of each, line by line; joint venturers have rights only to the net assets and equity-account the investment. Structure through a separate vehicle starts, not ends, the classification.

citation.ref: para 7 and 15-16

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 20 — Government grants
concepts.statement: A government grant is recognised only when there is reasonable assurance the entity will comply with its conditions and the grant will be received. Since the 2018 amendment, a grant related to an asset may be presented either as deferred income released over the asset's life, or by deducting it from the asset's carrying amount — the pre-2018 Indian text had removed the deduction option, and stale materials still teach that removal.

citation.ref: para 7 and 24 (as amended 2018)

concepts.section: Ind AS 101 First Time Adoption of Ind AS
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 101 — First-time adoption
concepts.statement: A first-time adopter may elect deemed cost for property, plant and equipment at the transition date: fair value at that date, or the previous GAAP carrying amount where eligible — instead of rebuilding depreciated cost as if Ind AS had always applied. The elections are optional exemptions from full retrospective application; the general rule remains retrospective, and mandatory exceptions forbid hindsight in estimates.

citation.ref: deemed cost exemption for PPE at transition

concepts.section: Ind AS 115 Revenue from Contracts with Customers
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 115 — Principal versus agent
concepts.statement: An entity is a principal when it controls the promised good or service before transfer to the customer, reporting gross revenue; an agent arranges for another to provide it, reporting only its fee or commission. Momentary legal title on the way through does not make a principal; inventory risk, primary responsibility for fulfilment and discretion in setting prices indicate control. The revenue difference is presentation, not profit.

citation.ref: para B34-B35

concepts.section: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 110 — Loss of control
concepts.statement: When a parent loses control of a subsidiary it derecognises the subsidiary's assets, liabilities and NCI, recognises the consideration received, and measures any retained interest at fair value at that date — that fair value becomes the cost of the new associate or investment. The gain or loss in profit or loss thus includes a remeasurement of the stake kept, not only the stake sold; control is an all-or-nothing line.

citation.ref: para 25

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 16 — Revaluation model
concepts.statement: Under the revaluation model an upward revaluation goes to other comprehensive income and accumulates in equity as revaluation surplus — except to the extent it reverses a decrease earlier charged to profit or loss. A downward revaluation charges profit or loss — except to the extent a surplus for that same asset exists to absorb it. The surplus never passes through profit or loss: on disposal it transfers directly to retained earnings.

citation.ref: para 39-40

concepts.section: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 2 — NRV and the raw materials exception
concepts.statement: Each line of inventory is carried at cost or at net realisable value, whichever is smaller, and that comparison is made item by item — but raw materials are not written down below cost while the finished products they will enter are expected to sell at or above cost. Only when the materials' price decline signals that the finished product's cost exceeds its NRV do the materials write down, with replacement cost as their best available measure.

citation.ref: para 32

concepts.subsection: Ind AS 41 — Agriculture
concepts.statement: Biological assets are measured at each reporting date at fair value less costs to sell, with changes through profit or loss — cost models yield to the market's verdict on living, growing assets. Bearer plants — the tea bush, not the tea leaf — are carved out to Ind AS 16 as plant-like assets, while the produce growing on them stays in Ind AS 41 until harvest, when it moves to Ind AS 2 at its harvest-date fair value as deemed cost.

citation.ref: para 12-13 and scope

concepts.subsection: Schedule III — Mandated ratios and disclosures
concepts.statement: Division II of Schedule III requires eleven named ratios in the notes — current ratio, debt-equity, debt service coverage, return on equity, inventory and receivables and payables turnover, net capital turnover, net profit, return on capital employed, return on investment — with the elements of each computation and an explanation wherever a ratio moved more than twenty-five per cent from the prior year. The amendments also demand disclosure of benami proceedings, undisclosed income surrendered, and crypto holdings.

citation.ref: Schedule III Division II (2021 amendments)

concepts.section: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 28 — Sharing an associate's losses
concepts.statement: Equity accounting absorbs an associate's losses only down to zero: once the investor's share of losses equals its interest — the equity-method carrying amount plus long-term interests that are in substance part of the net investment — recognition of further losses stops, resuming only after future profits rebuild the base. Losses beyond zero are provided only where the investor has legal or constructive obligations or made payments for the associate.

citation.ref: para 38-39

concepts.section: Ind AS 115 Revenue from Contracts with Customers
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 115 — Constraining variable consideration
concepts.statement: Variable consideration — bonuses, penalties, volume rebates, royalties — enters the transaction price only so far as the entity can say it is highly probable that no significant reversal of revenue already booked will follow once the uncertainty resolves. Estimation uses the expected value or the most likely amount, whichever predicts better; the constraint then trims the estimate. Booking the hopeful number and reversing later is the pattern the rule exists to stop.

citation.ref: para 56

concepts.section: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 7 — Cash and cash equivalents
concepts.statement: A cash equivalent is an investment held for the short term, easy to turn at short notice into a known sum of cash, and carrying insignificant risk that its value will shift — normally one maturing within about three months of acquisition. Equity investments are excluded save in-substance equivalents. Bank overdrafts repayable on demand that form an integral part of cash management join cash and cash equivalents, turning the statement's bottom line negative-capable.

citation.ref: para 7-8

concepts.section: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 110 — Consolidation procedures
concepts.statement: Consolidation combines like items line by line, eliminates the parent's investment against its share of each subsidiary's equity, and eliminates intragroup balances, transactions and unrealised profits in full — not merely the parent's share. The group reports as one economic entity under uniform accounting policies for like transactions, restating a subsidiary's numbers where its policies differ.

citation.ref: para 19 and B86

concepts.subsection: Chapter 6 of the FTP — Who may be an EOU, and the net foreign exchange test
concepts.statement: An Export Oriented Unit undertakes to export its entire production of goods and services, apart from the sales into the domestic tariff area that Chapter 6 itself permits, and it may be set up for manufacture, for repair, remaking, reconditioning and re-engineering, for services and software, and for agriculture, aquaculture, animal husbandry, floriculture, horticulture, poultry and sericulture. Trading units are outside the scheme altogether — the schemes buy export production, not export trading. Only a project with a minimum investment of one crore rupees in plant and machinery is considered for establishment as an EOU, and that floor does not apply to existing units, to units in an EHTP, STP or BTP, or to EOUs in agriculture, animal husbandry, aquaculture, brass hardware, floriculture, handicrafts, handmade jewellery, information technology and services; the Board of Approval may allow a lower floor besides. The obligation the whole scheme turns on is not a fixed export figure. The unit shall be a positive net foreign exchange earner, and the earning is computed cumulatively in blocks of five years beginning from the commencement of production, so a bad year is answered by the rest of its block rather than by a default. Where a product in the letter of permission is prohibited or restricted for export, the Board of Approval may extend that five year block; where the unit is in genuine hardship or an adverse market, it may extend it by up to one year, case by case. The unit executes a legal undertaking with the Development Commissioner, and failure to earn positive net foreign exchange or to keep the terms of the letter of permission exposes it to penal action under the Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act and to cancellation of that letter.

citation.ref: Paragraphs 6.00(a), 6.04, 6.05(c) and 6.06 of Chapter 6, read with Appendix 6B for the sector-specific value addition

concepts.subsection: Paragraph 6.07 — What an EOU may sell at home, and the four different conditions
concepts.statement: The rule is that the entire production of an EOU shall be exported; every domestic sale is an exception Chapter 6 grants, and the exceptions do not share one condition. Finished goods specified in the letter of permission, and the by-products, rejects, waste and scrap thrown off in making them, may be sold into the domestic tariff area only if they are freely importable under the policy and only on fulfilment of positive net foreign exchange, on payment of goods and services tax and compensation cess together with reversal of the customs duties that were availed as exemption on the inputs used in them, the reversal following the standard input output norms; an amount equal to the anti-dumping duty leviable at import is payable besides on those inputs, and pepper and pepper products and marble may not be sold domestically at all. For services, including software, the sale is capped instead of conditioned on the whole: up to fifty per cent of the free-on-board value of exports or fifty per cent of the foreign exchange earned. A gems and jewellery unit may sell up to ten per cent of the previous year's free-on-board value of exports, again on positive net foreign exchange. And two categories escape the net foreign exchange test entirely — sale of rejects up to five per cent of the free-on-board value of exports, and scrap, waste and remnants arising out of the production process, which are sold on the notified norms and applicable duties whatever the unit's net foreign exchange position. Reading one condition across all four is the mistake the paragraph is built to catch.

citation.ref: Paragraph 6.07(a) to (f) of Chapter 6

concepts.subsection: Paragraph 6.17 — Leaving the EOU scheme, and what the exit costs
concepts.statement: A unit may opt out of the scheme with the approval of the Development Commissioner, and the exit is priced: applicable excise and customs duties, and the integrated, central, State or union territory tax and compensation cess, all fall due, under the industrial policy in force. A unit that has not achieved its obligations is also liable to penalty at the time of exit — the duty is the price of the goods, the penalty is the price of the broken undertaking, and they are separate. The sequence matters as much as the sum. The unit intimates the Development Commissioner and the customs authorities in writing and assesses its own duty liability; customs confirm it on priority, on the condition that the unit has achieved positive net foreign exchange after taking the depreciation into account — which is also the only circumstance in which the depreciation benefit is available on capital goods disposed of into the domestic tariff area. The unit then obtains a No Dues Certificate, applies for final exit, and the Development Commissioner issues the final exit order within seven working days where nothing is pending under the Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act. In the gap between the No Dues Certificate and the final exit order the unit may claim no exemption for procuring capital goods or inputs, though an advance authorisation, a duty free import authorisation or duty drawback remain open to it on their own eligibility. Two conversions carry no duty on the way out: capital goods that a unit bought duty-paid as a domestic unit before converting into an EOU, and capital goods imported under EPCG whose export obligation was fully discharged before conversion.

citation.ref: Paragraph 6.17(a), (b), (d), (e) and (f) of Chapter 6, read with paragraph 6.14(b) on depreciation

concepts.subsection: Paragraphs 4.24 to 4.28 — Duty Free Import Authorisation, and how it is not an advance authorisation
concepts.statement: A Duty Free Import Authorisation lets an exporter import the inputs that went into goods he has already exported, and every one of its terms separates it from the advance authorisation it sits beside. It is issued on a post-export basis, and only for products for which standard input output norms have been notified, so there is no room for a self-declared norm. It exempts basic customs duty and nothing else — where an advance authorisation reaches the whole family of duties, this one reaches one of them, and the integrated tax and compensation cess are paid. Its minimum value addition is twenty per cent, against fifteen for an advance authorisation. It is transferable, and that is the sharpest difference of all: an advance authorisation and the material imported under it carry the actual user condition and cannot be transferred even after the export obligation is discharged, while the Regional Authority issues a transferable duty free import authorisation with a validity of twelve months from the date of issue, which will not be revalidated. The exports themselves must be completed within twelve months of filing the online application and generating the file number, a separate authorisation is issued for each set of norms, and no authorisation issues at all for an input carrying a pre-import condition or one for which the norms prescribe actual user. Import of tyres under the scheme is not allowed.

citation.ref: Paragraphs 4.24 to 4.28 of Chapter 4, read against paragraphs 4.09 and 4.16 for the advance authorisation comparison

concepts.subsection: Chapter 7 of the FTP — Deemed exports under the policy, which is not the GST list
concepts.statement: One phrase, two lists, in the same paper. For the Foreign Trade Policy, a deemed export is a transaction in which the goods do not leave the country, payment is received in Indian rupees or in free foreign exchange, and — the condition that does most of the work — the goods are manufactured in India. For the goods and services tax, Chapter 7 says in its own words that deemed exports mean only the supplies notified under section 147, on the Council's recommendation, with their own benefits and their own conditions. So a supply can be a deemed export for one of them and not the other, and answering a policy question out of section 147 is the trap. The policy's own categories are seven. A manufacturer's supply of goods against an advance authorisation or a duty free import authorisation; his supply to an EOU, STP, EHTP or BTP; and his supply of capital goods against an EPCG authorisation. And by a main or sub-contractor: supplies to projects funded by notified multilateral or bilateral agencies under international competitive bidding; supplies to projects the customs notification lets in at zero basic customs duty, again under such bidding, with mega power projects on their own terms; supplies to the United Nations or an approved international organisation; and supplies to a nuclear power project of 440 MW or more certified by a Joint Secretary in the Department of Atomic Energy and tendered competitively. The benefits are three, and only three: an advance authorisation or duty free import authorisation, deemed export drawback, and refund of terminal excise duty on the goods still in Schedule 4 of the Central Excise Act where the supply is eligible and no exemption already applies.

citation.ref: Paragraphs 7.01, 7.02 and 7.03 of Chapter 7, read with section 147 of the CGST Act, 2017 for the contrast the policy itself draws

concepts.subsection: Paragraphs 5.04(d), 5.09, 5.10 and 5.11 — Four ways to cut the export obligation, and why only one of them counts
concepts.statement: The specific export obligation is six times the duties, taxes and cess saved, and Chapter 5 offers four separate ways of cutting it. Where the capital goods are sourced from a domestic manufacturer the specific obligation is twenty-five per cent LESS. For an exporter of green technology products the specific obligation is seventy-five per cent OF the figure paragraph 5.01(b) gives. For a manufacturing unit in Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura, Jammu and Kashmir or Ladakh it is twenty-five per cent OF that figure, which is the largest cut of the four by a wide margin. And where the holder has fulfilled seventy-five per cent or more of the specific obligation together with the whole of the average obligation to date, in half or less than half the original period, the balance is condoned and the authorisation redeemed. Two things decide almost every question on this. First, the difference between twenty-five per cent less and twenty-five per cent of — one leaves three quarters standing and the other leaves a quarter. Second, paragraph 5.04(l): only ONE of these four benefits is admissible, so they are alternatives to choose between and never a stack to multiply together. None of the four touches the average export obligation, which each paragraph says in the same breath in which it grants the relief.

citation.ref: Paragraphs 5.04(d), 5.04(l), 5.09, 5.10 and 5.11 of Chapter 5, read with paragraph 5.01(b)

concepts.subsection: Paragraphs 5.04(c) and 5.12 — The average export obligation, which is a second obligation and not part of the first
concepts.statement: An EPCG holder carries two obligations at once and they are counted differently. The specific obligation is six times the duty saved over six years. The average export obligation is the arithmetic mean of what he exported of the same and similar products in the three preceding licensing years, and it must be met EVERY financial year until the specific obligation is complete, not once across the period. The two meet at one point that decides most questions: exports over and above the average are the only ones considered for fulfilment of the specific obligation, so a year that merely matches the past contributes nothing at all. Thirteen kinds of export are relieved of maintaining an average altogether — handicrafts, handlooms, industries covered by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission, agriculture, aquaculture including fisheries and pisciculture, animal husbandry and dairying, floriculture and horticulture, poultry, viticulture, sericulture, carpets, coir and jute. That relief is withdrawn for the import of fishing trawlers, boats, ships and similar items, so it turns on the item as well as on the sector. And goods other than tools imported by those sectors may not be transferred for five years from the date of import even where the export obligation has been fulfilled, which is a restriction that outlives the obligation it came with.

citation.ref: Paragraphs 5.04(c) and 5.12(a), (b) and (c) of Chapter 5

concepts.subsection: Paragraphs 5.01(d), 5.03 and 5.08 — How long the authorisation lives, and how long the condition on the machine does
concepts.statement: Three periods run at once under an EPCG authorisation and confusing them is the usual mistake. The authorisation is valid for IMPORT for twenty-four months from the date of its issue, and revalidation of an EPCG authorisation is not permitted at all, so capital goods not brought in inside that window cannot be brought in under it later. The export obligation runs for six years from the same date, which is a longer and quite separate clock. And the actual user condition on the imported capital goods runs until the export obligation is completed AND the Export Obligation Discharge Certificate is granted, so discharging the obligation in fact does not release the machine; the certificate does. How the obligation is measured also depends on where the goods came from: on a direct import it is reckoned on the duties, taxes and cess actually saved, while on domestic sourcing it is reckoned on the NOTIONAL customs duty, taxes and cess on the free-on-rail value shown in the Advance Release Order or invalidation letter. Where integrated tax and compensation cess are paid in cash on an import, that incidence is left out of the net duty saved provided input tax credit is not availed.

citation.ref: Paragraphs 5.01(d), 5.01(e), 5.03 and 5.08 of Chapter 5

concepts.section: Ind AS on Items impacting the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 12 — tax base, the temporary difference, and the balance it produces
concepts.statement: Deferred tax is arithmetic before it is judgement, and the arithmetic has four steps. Take what the balance sheet already carries the asset or the liability at. Take its tax base — for an asset, the amount deductible against taxable economic benefits in future periods; for a liability, its carrying amount less any amount that will be deductible in future periods. Subtract one from the other to get the temporary difference, and classify it — where an asset's carrying amount exceeds its tax base the difference is taxable and produces a deferred tax liability, and where it falls short the difference is deductible and produces a deferred tax asset, with the signs the other way round for a liability. Then multiply by the rate expected to apply when the difference reverses. Three things go wrong at this step more often than the rest put together. The balance sheet figure is the deferred tax balance at the year end, not the year's deferred tax expense, which is the movement between the opening and closing balances. The temporary difference is not itself the deferred tax — the rate still has to be applied. And deferred tax assets and liabilities are never discounted, however far away the reversal is.

citation.ref: the definitions of the tax base of an asset and of a liability, and the requirements that taxable temporary differences multiplied by the rate give deferred tax liabilities, that deductible temporary differences give deferred tax assets, and that deferred tax liabilities and assets are not discounted

concepts.section: Ind AS on Items impacting the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 12 — deferred tax on profit still sitting inside group inventory
concepts.statement: When one group company sells to another at a profit and the buyer still holds the goods at the year end, consolidation strips the profit out of inventory but the tax authorities do not. The seller has already paid tax on the sale, and the buyer's own tax return carries the goods at what it paid. So in the consolidated balance sheet the inventory's carrying amount is the original cost to the group while its tax base is the intra-group transfer price, and the tax base being the higher of the two makes the difference deductible — a deferred tax asset, not a liability. The measure of it is the profit still unrealised, which is the whole intra-group profit reduced in proportion to the goods sold on outside the group before the year end, not the whole profit and not the whole margin on the original sale. The asset is recognised where the buying company is expected to generate taxable profits to use it against, and it unwinds as the goods are sold outside the group, so the year's deferred tax movement is the change in the balance rather than the balance itself.

citation.ref: the example of a deductible temporary difference arising where unrealised profits on intragroup transactions are eliminated from the carrying amount of inventory with no equivalent adjustment for tax, read with the requirement that the tax base is determined by reference to the tax returns of each entity in the group while the carrying amount is taken from the consolidated financial statements

concepts.section: Ind AS on Items impacting the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 12 — the deferred tax on a fair value exercise, and what it does to goodwill
concepts.statement: A fair value exercise on an acquisition writes the acquiree's identifiable assets up to fair value in the consolidated financial statements while the tax authorities go on using the figures in the acquiree's own books. Every uplift with no equivalent tax adjustment is therefore a taxable temporary difference, and the deferred tax liability on it is recognised as one of the identifiable liabilities assumed at the acquisition date. That matters to the arithmetic in a way that is easy to miss — the liability reduces the identifiable net assets, so it increases goodwill or shrinks a bargain purchase gain by exactly the same amount. The order of work is fixed. Book net assets, plus the uplifts, less deferred tax at the rate expected to apply on the uplifts alone, gives net assets at fair value; consideration plus the non-controlling interest measured on whichever of the two permitted bases the group has chosen, less those net assets, gives goodwill. The one thing the standard will not let the arithmetic do is recognise a deferred tax liability on the initial recognition of the goodwill itself, which would only inflate the goodwill it was computed on.

citation.ref: the requirement that deferred tax assets and liabilities arising in a business combination are recognised as identifiable assets and liabilities at the acquisition date and so affect goodwill or the bargain purchase gain, together with the exception for the initial recognition of goodwill; read with Ind AS 103 paragraph 19 on the measurement of the non-controlling interest

concepts.section: Ind AS on Items impacting the Financial Statements
concepts.subsection: Ind AS 12 — which rate, and where the effect of a change in it goes
concepts.statement: Deferred tax is measured at whatever rate is expected to be in force for the period in which the asset gets realised or the liability gets settled, using rates and laws enacted, or substantively enacted, by the reporting date. Both halves bite.
