options.text: CA Shah and CA Menon — a retired partner belongs to the firm's own circle, and the room he keeps shows the connection has not been broken
options.misconception: treats a continuing association with the firm as partnership, when the clause turns on whether the person is a partner now
options.why: The clause asks one question about status. A member who has retired is not a partner, and the courtesy of an office is not a partnership deed. His signature on the firm's report would say that somebody is answerable for it who is not.

options.text: Only CA Shah — Clause 12 bars a member not being his partner from signing on the firm's behalf, and a retired partner and a partner of a network firm are both members who are not partners of this firm; CA Shah having done no work on the audit does not disqualify him, because the clause fixes who may sign and not who must have done the work
options.why: Clause 12 draws two lines around whoever puts the pen down. The person must be a member of the Institute who holds a certificate of practice; and he must be a partner of the member for whom he is signing, because the misconduct lies in letting a member not being his partner put a signature, for him or for his firm, on a balance sheet, a profit and loss account, a report or a set of financial statements. A retired partner is no longer a partner, and a partner of a network firm is a partner of a different firm however close the two are, so both are members not being his partner. CA Shah is a partner, which is what the clause asks. Who made the examination is a separate question answered by Clause 2 of Part I of the Second Schedule, and that clause permits the work to be done by a partner or an employee of the firm.
keywords: a member not being his partner

citation.ref: First Schedule, Part I, Clause 12 — the second limb, a member not being his partner

items.scenario: The firm's sole signing partner is in hospital and an audit report falls due. Three people offer to sign it on the firm's behalf. CA Menon retired from the firm's partnership two years ago and still keeps a room in its office. CA Dutt is a partner of another firm belonging to the same international network as this one. CA Shah is a partner of this firm who took no part at all in this audit.

items.stem: In which audit is the presumption properly rebutted?

options.text: Only the first — a single type of simple revenue transaction is the example SA 240 gives of circumstances in which the presumption is not applicable, while a complex revenue structure with a lack of controls over revenue recognition is where the risk is at its highest, and past honesty is no reason at all
options.why: SA 240 permits the presumption to be rebutted where it is not applicable in the circumstances of the engagement, and the Standard's own example is a single type of simple revenue transaction — leasehold revenue from a single unit rental property. The second file inverts the test. Where there is a complex revenue structure, or a lack of controls over revenue recognition, there is a high probability of fraud risk in revenue recognition, so those facts are reasons for the presumption to stand. Management's honesty in previous years is not among the circumstances the Standard contemplates, and the auditor keeps his skepticism regardless of it.
keywords: single type of simple revenue transaction

options.text: In both — the rebuttal is the auditor's own judgement, and a documented reason is all SA 240 asks for
options.misconception: treats the documentation requirement as the whole test, so any recorded reason is as good as any other
options.why: Documentation records a conclusion; it does not make one. What SA 240 asks the auditor to conclude is that the presumption is not applicable in the circumstances of the engagement, and a note saying management is honest does not reach that conclusion however carefully it is filed.

options.text: In neither — a rebuttal is open only where the entity has no revenue at all, which is why the Standard treats the risk as presumed
options.misconception: sets the bar at no revenue, when the Standard's own example is an entity that does have revenue of a single simple kind
options.why: An entity with no revenue would have nothing to presume about. The Standard's example is an entity with revenue of one simple kind, and the first audit here is exactly that.

options.text: In the second only — that auditor identified the complexity and the control weakness and dealt with them, while the first did no analysis of his revenue streams at all
options.misconception: reverses the test, treating complexity and weak controls as grounds for rebuttal rather than as the reasons the presumption stands
options.why: Identifying complexity and a lack of controls is the finding that keeps the presumption alive, not the finding that retires it. And the first auditor's revenue is a single lease, so there is one stream to analyse and he has analysed it.

citation.ref: para 26 and 47, with the example of circumstances in which the presumption of a risk of fraud in revenue recognition is not applicable

items.scenario: Two audits are reviewed. In the first, the entity's only revenue is rent from a single let property under one lease, invoiced monthly on fixed terms, and the file records that the presumed fraud risk in revenue recognition was rebutted. In the second, the entity earns revenue from four streams including corporate bookings, the team has itself found that the controls over revenue recognition are not designed to catch improper cut-off, and the file records that the presumption was rebutted because management has been honest in all previous years.

items.stem: What does SA 210 say about that paragraph?

options.text: It comes out, and so does the fresh engagement letter — a changed engagement continues to run under the letter originally signed
options.misconception: drops the requirement to record the changed terms, which SA 210 states separately from the rule about the report
options.why: The paragraph comes out and the letter stays. Once the terms have been changed, the auditor and management have to settle what the new ones are and set them down — in a fresh engagement letter, or in some other written form that does the same job.

options.text: It stays — the more a reader knows about the work behind a report, the better informed he is, and the change in terms ought to be disclosed to him
options.misconception: treats extra information as always helpful, when the extra information here invites reliance the review conclusion cannot carry
options.why: What the paragraph adds is not information about the review; it is a suggestion that the review rests on audit work. SA 210 keeps the two apart precisely so that a limited assurance conclusion is read as one.

options.text: It stays, because the change here had a reasonable justification; a paragraph of that kind is improper only where the engagement was downgraded without one
options.misconception: makes the rule about the reference depend on why the terms were changed, when it holds whatever the justification was
options.why: Justification and reporting are two separate requirements. A change with no reasonable justification is not agreed to at all; where it is agreed to, the report on the related service still carries no reference to the original engagement or its procedures.

options.text: It comes out — the report on the related service does not include reference to the original engagement or to any procedures performed in it, the one exception being an engagement changed to agreed-upon procedures, where reference to the procedures performed is a normal part of the report
options.why: SA 210 is careful about what the new report may say, because a review report that recites audit work invites the reader to take more comfort than the engagement now provides. The report on the related service does not include reference to the original engagement, nor to any procedures performed in the original audit engagement. The single exception is where the engagement has been changed to agreed-upon procedures, because there a description of the procedures performed is a normal part of the report and the reader is told in terms that no assurance is expressed.

citation.ref: para 16 and para 17, with the requirement that the report on the related service make no reference to the original engagement or to the procedures performed in it, except where the engagement is changed to agreed-upon procedures

items.scenario: Nine weeks into a voluntary audit the entity's circumstances change: a proposed listing is abandoned and the board now needs only a review for its bankers. You are satisfied that this is a change in circumstances affecting the entity's requirements, you agree to the change, and you and management record the new terms in a fresh engagement letter. Your manager then drafts the review report and, to show the depth of what was done, adds a paragraph stating that the engagement began as an audit and describing the audit procedures already performed.

items.stem: What does SA 260 require?

options.text: The three matters must be communicated, but the timing is a matter for the auditor, SA 260 fixing no date for any communication
options.misconception: reads the absence of a fixed date as an absence of any requirement about timing
options.why: No date is fixed and a standard is set instead: the auditor communicates with those charged with governance on a timely basis. A communication that arrives too late for the body to act on it fails that standard whatever the calendar says.

options.text: Whatever will shape the form and content of the auditor's report counts among the significant findings communicated to those charged with governance, so the intended qualification, the key audit matters and the going concern paragraph all go to the audit committee — and the communication is made on a timely basis, which a draft produced as the meeting opens is not
options.why: SA 260's list of significant findings from the audit reaches anything bearing on the form and content of the auditor's report he is about to sign, and all three of these bear on it in their own way: a qualification changes the opinion, a Key Audit Matters section is a part of the report, and a going concern paragraph is another. The committee is the body that oversees the financial reporting process, and it can only oversee something it hears about while it can still act. That is why the auditor communicates with those charged with governance on a timely basis rather than at the moment the report is signed.
keywords: form and content of the auditor's report

options.text: Nothing — the report is the auditor's own statement, and SA 260's list deals with matters arising in the audit rather than with what the report will eventually say
options.misconception: treats the report as outside the communication, when the standard's list names circumstances that affect its form and content
options.why: The list says otherwise in terms. Whatever will shape the form and content of the auditor's report sits inside it as a significant finding the standard requires to be communicated, and it is there because a governing body reading a qualification for the first time in the signed report has been deprived of its function.

options.text: Only the qualification needs to be communicated — key audit matters and a going concern paragraph do not modify the opinion, so they do not affect the form and content of the report
options.misconception: reads "form and content" as meaning a modification of the opinion alone, when it covers everything the report will contain
options.why: Form and content are wider than the opinion. A Key Audit Matters section and a Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern paragraph both change what the report looks like and what it tells a reader, and both are matters the committee needs to know are coming.

citation.ref: para 16 and para 21 — whatever shapes the form and content of the auditor's report is a significant finding from the audit, and it is communicated on a timely basis

items.scenario: The audit will end with a qualified opinion on inventory, a Key Audit Matters section naming revenue recognition, and a Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern paragraph. The engagement partner proposes to hand the audit committee the draft report on the morning of the board meeting at which the accounts are to be adopted, saying that what goes into the auditor's report is the auditor's own affair and that the committee will see it soon enough.

items.stem: What does SA 540 (Revised) require to be documented?

options.text: The indicators must be documented, but in summary only, the standard requiring documentation of significant judgements rather than of every observation made along the way
options.misconception: invents a summary standard, when the requirement names the indicators identified and the implications for the audit
options.why: The requirement is specific about two things: the indicators of possible management bias identified during the audit, and the implications for the audit. A summary that names neither leaves the reviewer no way of telling what was seen.

options.text: The indicators need be documented only where the auditor concludes that the estimates are misstated, since it is then that they explain the modification
options.misconception: makes the documentation requirement follow the outcome, when it follows the identification of the indicators
options.why: If the requirement ran only where the estimates were misstated it would never reach the case it was written for. The standard's own point is that judgements can be individually reasonable and still be indicators of possible management bias, and that is exactly the file this senior wants to leave silent.

options.text: The indicators of possible management bias identified during the audit and the implications for the audit both go into the audit documentation, whatever the conclusion reached on the reasonableness of the estimates
options.why: The requirement follows the identification, not the outcome. SA 540 (Revised) has the auditor include in the audit documentation the indicators of possible management bias identified during the audit and the implications for the audit, which is what allows anyone reading the file to see that the pattern was noticed and weighed rather than missed. A conclusion recorded with the reasoning stripped out of it does not show how it was reached, and the indicators are the reasoning here.

options.text: Only the conclusion — indicators that did not turn into misstatements are not audit evidence and have no place in the file
options.misconception: treats what was considered and set aside as not worth recording, when the file is meant to show how the conclusion was reached
options.why: Documentation records the work as well as the result. The indicators are what the auditor weighed in reaching the conclusion that the estimates are reasonable, and a file that shows only the conclusion cannot be reviewed against the judgement that produced it.

citation.ref: the audit documentation requirement — indicators of possible management bias identified during the audit and the implications for the audit

items.scenario: You identified a pattern of accounting estimates all leaning the same way, evaluated it, and concluded that every estimate falls inside a supportable range and that the financial statements are not misstated in respect of them. The senior proposes to record in the file only the conclusion that the estimates are reasonable, saying that indicators of bias which led nowhere would only invite questions from a reviewer or a regulator later on.

items.stem: What comes first, and why is the engagement team told at all?

options.text: Nothing happens until management confirms the relationship, since management identifies related parties and the auditor's role is to test what it has identified
options.misconception: leaves the determination to the party whose own list is in question
options.why: The list was silent about this party, which is the whole difficulty. The determination whether the underlying circumstances confirm the existence of the relationship is the auditor's, and management is then asked to identify all transactions with the party for his further evaluation.

options.text: The team is told so that the extra work can be shared out and the additional procedures properly staffed before the deadline
options.misconception: reads a risk-assessment communication as a resourcing message, so the point of telling the team is lost
options.why: Staffing follows, but it is not why the standard requires the communication. The reason given is that the other members may need to reconsider what their own procedures have already produced, because a related party discovered late can change what earlier work is worth.

options.text: First decide whether the underlying circumstances confirm that a related party relationship or transaction is really there, an arrangement that merely hints at one not yet being one — and the rest of the engagement team is told promptly so that each of them can ask whether what has surfaced unsettles the results of, and the conclusions reached from, the risk assessment work already done, and whether the assessed risk of material misstatement now has to be looked at again
options.why: SA 550 puts a threshold in front of the steps. Something surfaces — an arrangement, or a piece of information — pointing towards a related party that management's own list never named. The auditor's first move is to ask whether the underlying circumstances confirm the existence of a relationship or a transaction of that kind, because a similar name is a reason to look and not yet a related party. The standard also says why the rest of the engagement team hears about it without delay: so that its other members can weigh whether what has surfaced unsettles the results of, and the conclusions reached from, risk assessment procedures already performed, and whether the assessed risk of material misstatement now has to be reassessed.

options.text: The six steps begin at once — SA 550 sets no threshold, and a suspicion strong enough to notice is strong enough to act on
options.misconception: skips the determination the standard puts first, so the steps run on a resemblance that may turn out to be nothing
options.why: There is a threshold and it is stated. The auditor determines whether the underlying circumstances confirm the existence of the relationship or transaction, and the steps that follow — requesting management, inquiring into the controls, substantive procedures — are for a party the circumstances have confirmed.

citation.ref: para 22 — the determination whether the underlying circumstances confirm the existence of the relationship or transaction, and the purpose of the prompt communication to the other members of the engagement team

items.scenario: Inspecting bank confirmations you see a guarantee the company has given for a loan taken by Meghna Enterprises, a name that appears nowhere on management's related party list. The name resembles that of a business the managing director's spouse is said to run, but you have nothing yet beyond the resemblance. The senior proposes to start the SA 550 steps at once — write to the engagement team, ask management for all transactions with Meghna Enterprises, and inquire why the controls failed to identify it.

items.stem: Which engagement fits what the company has described?

options.text: An audit — anything short of reasonable assurance is of no practical use to a lender, and the company's preference for a negative conclusion cannot lower the standard
options.misconception: treats the audit as the only engagement worth having, when the framework provides a middle rung for exactly this need
options.why: Lenders use review reports routinely for interim and half-yearly figures. The question is what level of assurance the user needs and is asking for, and here the user has said what it needs and it is less than an audit.

options.text: A review, but with the conclusion expressed positively, since what the lender ultimately wants to know is that the statements are right
options.misconception: keeps a review's procedures and borrows an audit's form of conclusion, so the report says more than the work supports
options.why: The negative form is not a stylistic habit; it is what limited assurance can honestly carry. A positive conclusion asserts that the practitioner has obtained enough evidence to say the statements are right, which inquiry and analytical procedures alone do not provide.

options.text: An agreed-upon procedures engagement — it is the cheapest of the three, and the report can be worded so that nothing came to the practitioner's attention
options.misconception: buys the cheapest engagement and then borrows a review's wording for it, which is the misdescription the ladder exists to prevent
options.why: The wording is not free to move between engagements. An agreed-upon procedures report states factual findings on named procedures and says expressly that it is not an audit or a review and that no assurance is expressed; a sentence borrowed from a review would promise the lender something the work never produced.

options.text: A review — it gives limited assurance on the financial statements as a whole, is built mainly on inquiry and analytical procedures, and its conclusion is expressed in the negative form; an agreed-upon procedures engagement gives no assurance at all and says nothing about the statements as a whole, and an audit's reasonable assurance is more than the company has asked for
options.why: The three engagements sit on a ladder and the company has described the middle rung. A review gives limited assurance across the financial statements, working mainly through inquiry and analytical procedures, and it concludes in the negative form: nothing came to the practitioner's attention that would make him think the financial statements fail, in any material respect, to follow the framework they are drawn up under. An agreed-upon procedures engagement gives no assurance at all and reports factual findings on the specified procedures only, so it can say nothing about the statements as a whole. An audit would answer the need, and would cost more than the need.

citation.ref: Ch. Related Services, read with Ch. Review of Financial Information — the level of assurance and the form of conclusion in a review and in an agreed-upon procedures engagement

items.scenario: A company must give its lender comfort on a full set of half-yearly financial statements. No statute requires those statements to be audited. The company wants the least expensive engagement that still lets the lender take a view on the statements as a whole, and it has told the lender it will accept a conclusion worded in the negative.

items.stem: What is required?

options.text: The opinion is not modified by the CARO answer — the CARO report is a separate statement annexed to the auditor's report, and whether the opinion is modified is decided under SA 570 and SA 705 — but where the answer to any CARO question is unfavourable or qualified, the auditor's report must also state the basis for that answer, so a bare "no" will not do
options.why: Two documents and two questions. The CARO report is a separate statement annexed to the auditor's report, and answering one of its clauses unfavourably is not itself a modification of the opinion; whether the opinion is modified is settled under SA 570 and, if it comes to it, SA 705, and here the disclosure is adequate so the opinion stands unmodified with the Material Uncertainty section. What CARO adds is a duty of explanation. An answer that comes out unfavourable or qualified cannot be left standing bare: the auditor's report has to state the basis on which he gave it.

options.text: The opinion stands unmodified and a bare "no" is enough — CARO calls for an answer to each question, not for the auditor's reasons
options.misconception: answers the clause and stops, missing the requirement that an unfavourable answer carry its basis
options.why: The first half is right and the second is not. CARO requires that where the answer to any of its questions is unfavourable or qualified, the report shall also state the basis for that answer, which is what makes the annexure readable by anyone but its author.

options.text: An unfavourable answer to clause 3(xix) requires the opinion to be qualified, the clause and the going concern conclusion being about the same thing
options.misconception: treats a CARO answer as though it were part of the opinion, so one unfavourable clause drags the opinion with it
options.why: They are not the same thing and they do not sit in the same document. Clause 3(xix) asks its own question on its own named inputs and is answered in an annexure; the opinion on the financial statements is formed under the standards and is modified only when they require it.

options.text: The clause cannot be answered unfavourably at all where the going concern basis has been found appropriate, since a company that is a going concern is by definition capable of meeting its liabilities
options.misconception: collapses the clause into the SA 570 conclusion, when the clause asks a differently worded question anchored to the balance sheet date
options.why: The going concern basis being appropriate and no material uncertainty existing are different findings — SA 570 provides for a Material Uncertainty section precisely for the case where both an appropriate basis and a material uncertainty exist together. Clause 3(xix) puts a question of its own: on the ratios, the ageing and the plans it names, does the auditor take the view that no material uncertainty hangs over the company's ability to pay off the liabilities standing in its balance sheet as they come due across the following year? That question can be answered unfavourably on an appropriate going concern basis.

citation.ref: paragraph 3(xix), read with paragraph 4 requiring the auditor's report to state the basis for any unfavourable or qualified answer

items.scenario: You conclude under clause 3(xix) that a material uncertainty does exist. Separately, under SA 570 you conclude that the going concern basis is appropriate and that the disclosure of the uncertainty in the notes is adequate, so you include a Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern section and your opinion is unmodified. The engagement partner asks whether an unfavourable answer to the clause forces the opinion to be modified, and whether a bare "no" in the CARO annexure is enough.

items.stem: What does clause 3(xx) actually report on?

options.text: Report both limbs adversely, clause 3(xx) covering compliance with section 135 as a whole
options.misconception: reads a two-limbed clause about transfers as a general compliance check on the whole of section 135
options.why: The clause is narrower than the section it sits under. It has exactly two questions, both about the transfer of an unspent amount to a stated destination within a stated window, and neither is a general audit of how the money was spent.

options.text: Report clause 3(xx)(b) adversely, because money handed to an unregistered implementing agency has not reached its ongoing project and is therefore unspent for the purpose of section 135(6)
options.misconception: converts a spending irregularity into an unspent amount, when the second limb asks only whether an amount remaining unspent pursuant to an ongoing project reached the special account
options.why: Section 135(6) deals with an amount remaining unspent at the end of the financial year in respect of an ongoing project, which is transferred to the special account within thirty days of the year end. Money paid out to an agency has been spent, well or badly, and the second limb has nothing to say about the choice of agency.

options.text: Report clause 3(xx)(a) adversely — money spent on an activity outside Schedule VII is in substance unspent corporate social responsibility money, whatever the cash book shows
options.misconception: rewrites improper spending as an unspent amount, so a clause about a transfer is used to report a different failure
options.why: Clause 3(xx)(a) asks whether an unspent amount was transferred to a Fund specified in Schedule VII. The company transferred nothing because it had nothing unspent, and deeming the misspent money to be unspent would make the clause report something it never asks about.

options.text: Neither limb has anything to report — both ask only whether an unspent amount was transferred, one to a Fund specified in Schedule VII and the other to the special account, and nothing here was unspent; the propriety of the spending is a section 135 compliance question answered elsewhere in your reporting, not inside clause 3(xx)
options.why: Read the two limbs as they are written. Clause 3(xx)(a) asks whether, in respect of other than ongoing projects, the unspent amount was transferred to a Fund specified in Schedule VII within six months of the expiry of the financial year. Clause 3(xx)(b) asks whether any amount remaining unspent pursuant to an ongoing project was transferred to the special account under section 135(6). Both are questions about whether an unspent amount was transferred, and a company that spent everything has no unspent amount to transfer. That the money went to the wrong activity and through an unregistered agency is a real failure, but the propriety of the spending is not what either limb asks about; it belongs where compliance with section 135 is reported.

citation.ref: paragraph 3(xx)(a) and 3(xx)(b), with the second proviso to section 135(5) and section 135(6) of the Companies Act, 2013

items.scenario: A company met its whole corporate social responsibility obligation in cash during the year, so nothing at all was left unspent. On examination you find that a large part of the money was spent on a programme that is not an activity specified in Schedule VII, and that a further part went to an implementing agency which is not registered as the CSR Rules require. The audit committee asks whether clause 3(xx) must therefore be reported adversely.

items.stem: Is that right?

options.text: No — the first limb asks whether there is in place an internal audit system commensurate with the size and nature of what this company does, and a system run by an outside firm covering every location on a defined cycle is such a system; who employs the internal auditor is not what the limb asks about
options.why: The clause asks about a system and about its fit, not about a payroll. An internal audit system commensurate with the size and nature of the business can be staffed by the company's own employees, by an outside firm engaged for the purpose, or by a mixture, and the question in every case is whether the coverage matches what this company is and does. Here it does. Who employs the internal auditor decides nothing under this limb, and answering "no" would tell a reader something about the company that is not true.
keywords: internal audit system commensurate with the size and nature

options.text: No, but the second limb must then be answered "no" as well, since the reports of an outside firm are not reports of the Internal Auditors
options.misconception: reads "Internal Auditors" in the second limb as meaning employees, so a properly considered set of reports goes unreported
options.why: The second limb asks one thing of the statutory auditor: did he take the internal auditors' reports for the period he was auditing into account? The outside firm is the internal auditor here, its reports cover that period, and they are on the file and have been read.

options.text: Yes — an internal audit system means a function inside the company, and an engagement bought from an outside firm is a professional service rather than a system
options.misconception: reads "internal" as describing who is employed rather than what is examined
options.why: Internal describes the subject matter, not the contract of employment. The function examines the company's own activities as a service to the company, and it does that whether the people performing it are on the payroll or engaged from outside.

options.text: No — and because the arrangement is an outsourced one, the first limb is answered by the scope set out in the outside firm's engagement letter, without any separate test of whether the coverage matched the company's size and nature
options.misconception: substitutes the contracted scope for the judgement about fit that the limb actually calls for
options.why: An engagement letter says what was promised. The limb asks whether what the company has is commensurate with the size and nature of its business, which is answered by looking at the coverage delivered against the operations that exist, whoever wrote the scope.

citation.ref: paragraph 3(xiv)(a) and 3(xiv)(b)

items.scenario: A company has no internal audit department of its own. Its internal audit is carried out by an outside firm of chartered accountants engaged for the purpose, which covers every location on a defined cycle; its reports for the whole of the period under audit are on your file and you have read them. The audit senior proposes to answer clause 3(xiv)(a) "no", on the ground that a company which employs no internal auditor has no internal audit system.

items.stem: What must the parent's auditor obtain from those component auditors before that reliance?

options.text: The component auditors' complete working paper files, since the parent's auditor cannot rely on a report he has not verified for himself
options.misconception: turns reliance on another auditor into re-performance of his audit, which is not what the framework asks for
options.why: The parent's auditor is not required to re-audit the components, and his opinion in respect of them is expressly stated to be based solely on the other auditors' reports. What he obtains are confirmations and the information he needs for the consolidation and the disclosures.

options.text: Nothing further — the reports have been furnished, and the Other Matter paragraph records that the opinion in respect of those amounts rests solely on them
options.misconception: treats the disclosure of reliance as the justification for it, so the paragraph does the work the confirmations were meant to do
options.why: Recording a reliance and being entitled to it are two different things. The confirmations as to independence and compliance with the code of ethics are what make the other auditors' reports usable, and the paragraph tells the reader what was done, not whether it was proper.

options.text: Confirmations from the component auditors as to their independence and their compliance with the code of ethics, together with the information required for the consolidation and for the disclosure requirements — the Other Matter paragraph discloses how the work was divided and does not by itself create the entitlement to rely on another auditor's report
options.why: A report arriving through the client's post room is not, by itself, a basis for an opinion. The parent's auditor obtains certain confirmations from the component auditors — as to their independence and their compliance with the code of ethics, and the information required for the consolidation and for the disclosure requirements. Only then does his opinion, in so far as it relates to those components, rest on their reports. The Other Matter paragraph is the disclosure that follows; it records how the work was divided and cannot supply what the division depends on.
keywords: compliance with the code of ethics

options.text: A written representation from the management of the holding company that the component auditors were independent and complied with ethical requirements
options.misconception: takes from management a confirmation that only the component auditors themselves can give
options.why: Management does not know whether another firm was independent and cannot be the source of that assurance. The confirmations come from the component auditors, and a representation from the parent's management about somebody else's independence is worth nothing on the point.

citation.source: Guidance Note on Audit of Consolidated Financial Statements
citation.ref: the confirmations the parent's auditor obtains from component auditors as to independence and compliance with the code of ethics and the information required for the consolidation and disclosures, read with the Other Matter paragraph stating that his opinion on the amounts in respect of those components is based solely on the reports of the other auditors

items.scenario: Three of the group's components were audited by other auditors, and their reports have been furnished to you by the management of the holding company. Your manager has drafted the Other Matter paragraph giving the number of those components and the amounts they represent, and proposes to sign, saying that once the reports are on the file the opinion in respect of those amounts may be based solely on them.

items.stem: What route does the long form audit report actually take?

options.text: To the bank's management, whose acceptance of the comments closes the matter; the Board and the Reserve Bank see only the statutory audit report
options.misconception: treats management's acceptance as the end of the route, when the report is placed before the Board's committee and copied to the regulator
options.why: Management is one stop, not the last. The report is placed before the Audit Committee of the Board with the action taken or proposed, and a copy with the Board's views or directions goes to the Reserve Bank.

options.text: Straight from the branch to the Reserve Bank, the long form audit report being a return the regulator prescribes and the branch answers
options.misconception: sends the report to the regulator without the bank's own governance ever seeing it, which is the step the whole route exists for
options.why: What the Reserve Bank wants is not only the report but the bank's answer to it. That is why the report reaches the Audit Committee of the Board first and goes on with the Board's views or directions and a note about what will be done.

options.text: Branch auditors hand their long form audit reports up to the statutory central auditors, who consolidate them at head office and give the bank-level long form audit report to management; management puts it before the Audit Committee of the Board, which says what has been done or will be done to put the irregularities right; and within sixty days of the statutory auditors submitting it, the Reserve Bank gets a copy along with the relative agenda note and whatever views or directions the Board has recorded
options.why: The report climbs the bank before it leaves it. Each branch auditor's long form audit report travels up to the statutory central auditors, and once the consolidation is done at head office the bank-level report passes to management. Management then lays it, duly examined, before the Audit Committee of the Board, which records what has been done or is to be done to set the irregularities right. Sixty days from the day the statutory auditors submit their report, a copy of it reaches the Reserve Bank, and with it go the relative agenda note and whatever views or directions the Board has given.
keywords: consolidation is done at head office

options.text: To the statutory central auditors and no further — the consolidated long form audit report is a working paper supporting their own report on the bank
options.misconception: stops the route at the central auditors, so the report never reaches management, the Board or the regulator
options.why: The consolidated report is submitted by the statutory central auditors to management, placed before the Audit Committee of the Board, and copied to the Reserve Bank. A document with that journey is not a working paper.

citation.ref: Ch. Audit of Banks — the long form audit report given by statutory branch auditors and statutory central auditors, its consolidation at head office, its placing before the Audit Committee of the Board, and the copy submitted to the Reserve Bank within sixty days

items.scenario: A branch auditor has finished his long form audit report. His assistant asks where it goes now. The branch manager says the branch will send it straight to the Reserve Bank, the long form audit report being a Reserve Bank requirement, and that once it is with the regulator nothing further has to happen inside the bank.

items.stem: Whose recommendations do these facts engage?

options.text: The Ghosh Committee's, but the auditor's only duty is to report the unreconciled balances as a weakness in the branch's own records, the long form audit report asking about implementation rather than about balances
options.misconception: separates the balances from the recommendation they answer, when the balances are the evidence that the recommendation is not implemented
options.why: The two are the same finding. What the long form audit report asks is whether the recommendation on prompt reconciliation has been implemented, and a year-old outstanding entry in the inter-branch account is how the auditor knows it has not.

options.text: The Jilani Committee's — reconciliation is an internal control matter, and the internal control system was that committee's subject
options.misconception: sorts by the words "internal control" rather than by what each committee actually dealt with
options.why: The Jilani Committee dealt with the internal control and inspection or audit system in banks — the machinery that checks: an independent inspection department, the inspection cycle, concurrent audit and the rectification of irregularities. Reconciliation of inter-branch, nostro and suspense accounts is anti-fraud housekeeping, and it is Ghosh's.

options.text: Neither — the two committees dealt with custody, staff rotation, inspection cycles and concurrent audit, and reconciliation appears in neither set of recommendations
options.misconception: remembers each committee by two or three headline items and treats the rest of its recommendations as not existing
options.why: Prompt reconciliation of inter-branch accounts, nostro accounts and suspense and sundry accounts is a Ghosh Committee recommendation. Learning a committee by its most quoted items leaves gaps in exactly the places an examiner reaches for.

options.text: The Ghosh Committee's — its recommendations on frauds and malpractices in banks include the prompt reconciliation of inter-branch accounts, of nostro accounts and of suspense and sundry accounts, and the auditor reports on the implementation of them in the long form audit report
options.why: The Ghosh Committee dealt with frauds and malpractices in banks, and its recommendations run wider than custody and staff. Prompt reconciliation of inter-branch accounts, of nostro accounts and of suspense and sundry accounts is among them, and the reason is exactly the one the manager denies: an account nobody reconciles is where a fraud can sit undisturbed, because the entry that would expose it is never matched against anything. A year-old outstanding entry is therefore a recommendation not implemented, and the auditor reports on the implementation of the recommendations in the long form audit report.

citation.ref: Ch. Audit of Banks — the Ghosh Committee on frauds and malpractices in banks, including prompt reconciliation of inter-branch, nostro and suspense and sundry accounts, and the reporting on implementation in the long form audit report

items.scenario: At the branch you find entries outstanding for more than a year in the inter-branch account and in the suspense and sundry accounts, and nostro balances that have not been reconciled at all this year. The branch manager says these are back-office housekeeping matters with no bearing on frauds, and that the committee whose recommendations deal with frauds is concerned with custody, staff rotation and security stationery, none of which is in issue here.

items.stem: How are the two matters actually reported?

options.text: In the observations or qualifications paragraph of Form 3CA — the report states that the particulars given in Form 3CD are true and correct subject to the observations or qualifications set out there, so the particulars themselves are stated in Form 3CD and the auditor's reservation is carried in that paragraph of the report
options.why: The report and the annexure do different jobs and neither is left blank. Form 3CD carries the particulars, stated as best the auditor can state them. Form 3CA is the report that covers them, and it says that in the auditor's opinion and to the best of his information and according to the explanations given to him the particulars given in Form 3CD are true and correct, subject to the observations or qualifications set out in that paragraph. An unverified particular and a disputed value both go there, where a reader looking for the auditor's reservations will find them.

options.text: In a note to the financial statements, the tax auditor having no place of his own in which to record a reservation
options.misconception: puts the auditor's reservation into the assessee's own statements, where the assessee controls the wording
options.why: The auditor has a place of his own and it is in his report. A note in the financial statements is the assessee's statement about itself; the observations or qualifications paragraph is the auditor's statement about the particulars.

options.text: In the opinion paragraph of Form 3CB, since a reservation about the particulars is a reservation about the accounts from which they are drawn
options.misconception: reaches for the form used where no other audit exists, and turns a reservation on particulars into a reservation on the accounts
options.why: Form 3CB is used where the accounts are not audited under any other law, and this company's are. The tax auditor here reports in Form 3CA, and the reservation belongs in that report's observations or qualifications paragraph rather than in an opinion on accounts another auditor has already opined on.

options.text: Leave the two particulars blank in Form 3CD, a blank being the recognised way of showing that the auditor could not verify or could not agree
options.misconception: uses silence to carry a reservation, which leaves the reader unable to tell an omission from a disagreement
options.why: A blank says nothing about why it is blank. The form provides a paragraph for observations or qualifications precisely so that the auditor can state what he could not verify and what he does not agree with, in words.

citation.ref: Section 44AB with Rule 6G — Form 3CA and Form 3CB, and the observations or qualifications paragraph in which the auditor states his reservations on the particulars given in Form 3CD

items.scenario: In the tax audit of a company whose statutory audit under the Companies Act is complete, you cannot verify a particular required by one clause of Form 3CD, and you disagree with the assessee on the value stated under another. The article assistant proposes two fixes: leave both particulars blank in Form 3CD, and attach a covering letter to the return explaining why.

items.stem: How should clause 3(xviii) be answered?

options.text: Leave it blank — the reportable matter is the concerns raised by the outgoing auditor, and where he raised none there is nothing to report
options.misconception: collapses the clause's two limbs into the second one, so a clean resignation disappears from the report entirely
options.why: The two limbs are separate and the first stands on its own. Whether there has been any resignation is reported whatever the answer to the second limb, and "there was a resignation and no issues, objections or concerns were raised" is a materially different statement to a reader from silence.
keywords: whatever the answer to the second limb

options.text: It must be answered, not left blank — the clause is engaged by any resignation of the statutory auditors during the year whatever the reason for it, and the answer states that there was a resignation and that you took into consideration the issues, objections or concerns raised by the outgoing auditor, of which there were none
options.why: The clause asks two things in sequence. First comes the plain question: was there any resignation of the statutory auditors during the year? Nothing in it turns on whether the exit was friendly — a retirement, a firm winding up and a dispute all answer that question the same way. The second limb then asks what the incoming auditor did with the issues, objections or concerns his predecessor put to him, and the honest answer where none were put is to say so, which is a report and not a blank.
keywords: any resignation of the statutory auditors during the year

options.text: It is answered by the outgoing auditor rather than by you, since only he knows what he raised and why he left
options.misconception: hands a clause of the incoming auditor's own report to the auditor who has left office
options.why: CARO 2020 is an annexure to the report of the auditor now in office, and clause 3(xviii) is his statement about a predecessor. The outgoing auditor has his own and quite separate obligation, which is the statement he files under section 140(2); it is not this clause and it does not answer it.

options.text: Leave it blank — a resignation caused by a firm winding up is a cessation of office rather than a resignation, so the clause is not engaged
options.misconception: reads a reason into a clause that asks only whether a resignation happened
options.why: The clause contains no test of cause. The auditor left office by resigning, and the resignation is the fact reported; inventing a category of exits the clause does not reach leaves the reader with no information at all about a change the annexure exists to surface.

citation.ref: paragraph 3(xviii)

items.scenario: The previous statutory auditor resigned in September. The reason was that his firm's sole partner retired and the firm wound up; he wrote to you saying so, adding that he had raised nothing with the company and had no concerns of any kind, and you found none. You communicated with him in writing before accepting, and he confirmed he had no objection. Drafting the CARO annexure, the senior proposes to leave clause 3(xviii) blank on the ground that the clause is aimed at auditors who leave under a cloud, and nothing of that sort happened.

items.stem: What does the guidance require before that question arises?

options.text: Every component's figures have to be audited, or at the least put through audit procedures, that being how a group audit spread across many locations is meant to work; and either the group's own auditor or a component's auditor may do that work — so the first step is to perform procedures on the three yourself or arrange for them, and only what genuinely remains unaudited then goes into the evaluation of a possible modification
options.why: The reporting question is the second question, not the first. Every component's figures are either audited or, short of that, subjected to audit procedures, that being how a multi-location group audit is meant to work; and the work goes to whoever is placed to do it — the auditor reporting on the consolidated financial statements, or each component's own auditor. Access to one shared system makes that practicable here. Only for whatever is left over after that does the auditor weigh qualitative and quantitative factors on the possible effect of the amounts remaining unaudited, and consider a modification under SA 705.
keywords: auditor reporting on the consolidated financial statements
possible effect of the amounts remaining unaudited

options.text: Obtain the parent's internal audit reports on the three entities, which supply the audit the components never had
options.misconception: treats the internal audit function's reports as the audit or the audit procedures the guidance asks for, and skips the gates SA 610 sets before that work may be used at all
options.why: Internal audit work is not an audit of the component and does not become one by being filed. Whether any of it may be used at all is decided under SA 610 (Revised), on the function's objectivity, competence and systematic and disciplined approach, and even where it may be used the group auditor still performs his own procedures on the body of work.
keywords: not an audit of the component

options.text: Nothing comes before it — an unaudited component is an inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence, and the only live question is qualified or disclaimer
options.misconception: treats the evidence gap as fixed and unclosable, when the auditor reporting on the group may close it himself
options.why: It becomes an inability only if it stays unaudited. Treating it as settled at the moment it is noticed skips the step where the group auditor performs the procedures, and turns a working problem into a reporting problem before anyone has tried to solve it.

options.text: Ask the parent to leave the three entities out of the consolidation until they have been audited, and disclose the exclusion in the notes
options.misconception: converts a shortage of audit evidence into an exemption from consolidation
options.why: Whether an entity is consolidated is decided by the applicable accounting standards on control, not by whether anyone has audited it. Leaving a controlled entity out because it is unaudited misstates the consolidated financial statements instead of auditing them.

citation.source: Guidance Note on Audit of Consolidated Financial Statements (Revised 2016)
citation.ref: Components not audited — the requirement that all components be audited or subjected to audit procedures in a multi-location group audit, and the evaluation of a possible modification under SA 705 for what remains unaudited

items.scenario: A group consolidates eleven components. Three of them are small overseas selling entities in jurisdictions where no statutory audit is required, and none has ever been audited. You are the auditor reporting on the consolidated financial statements, the group's records are all kept on one system to which you have access, and the three entities together carry 7 per cent of consolidated revenue. The manager opens the file note with "the only question is whether we qualify or disclaim".

items.stem: What do SA 580 and the guidance on consolidated financial statements require here?

options.text: No acknowledgement of responsibility is needed from the parent at all, each component's management having already acknowledged responsibility for its own financial statements to its own auditor
options.misconception: adds up component-level acknowledgements and treats the sum as covering a set of statements no component's management ever prepared
options.why: Nobody but the parent's management prepares the consolidated financial statements — it identifies the components, obtains their information, makes the consolidation adjustments and harmonises the policies — so nobody but the parent's management can acknowledge responsibility for them.

options.text: The draft is acceptable, because the group chief financial officer's signature binds the parent's management and a signature is what a written representation is for
options.misconception: treats the identity of the signatory as curing what the letter actually says
options.why: Who signs does not change what is being represented. A correctly signed letter acknowledging responsibility for the wrong statements under the wrong framework, and silent on approval, is a letter that fixes management's position on matters the auditor did not ask about.

options.text: The draft is right on the framework — a group with components on different frameworks cannot represent about a single one — but wrong on approval, which the audit committee has given
options.misconception: lets the components' own frameworks decide what the parent represents about, and treats a committee's noting as the board's approval
options.why: The consolidated financial statements are prepared under one framework, the parent's, and a component on a different framework is dealt with by conversion before consolidation rather than by splitting the representation. Noting is not approving, and the representation the auditor seeks is that the statements have been approved.

options.text: What the parent's management must acknowledge is its own responsibility for the consolidated financial statements — a true and fair presentation of them, drawn up under the reporting framework the parent itself reports in; and the auditor must separately obtain evidence that the parent's management has approved those consolidated financial statements
options.why: Two things are wrong with the draft. The subject of the acknowledgement is the consolidated financial statements, not each component's own, and the framework named is the financial reporting framework applicable to the parent — which is the framework the consolidated statements are actually prepared under, whatever books a component keeps. And approval is a second and separate representation: the auditor obtains evidence that parent management has approved the consolidated financial statements, which noting by a committee is not.
keywords: financial reporting framework applicable to the parent

citation.ref: Ch. Group Audits — what the parent's management acknowledges about the consolidated statements it has prepared, which framework those statements are drawn up under, and its approval of them, read with SA 580

items.scenario: An Indian parent reporting under Ind AS consolidates a US subsidiary that keeps its own books under US GAAP. The draft representation letter has the parent's management acknowledging its responsibility "for a true and fair presentation of each component's financial statements in accordance with the framework applicable to that component". The letter is signed by the group chief financial officer. The consolidated financial statements have not yet been put to the parent's board; the audit committee has seen and noted them.

items.stem: Is the partner right?

options.text: No, but only because of the regulator's new report — growth in the business and a misunderstanding of scope are matters for the audit strategy rather than for the terms
options.misconception: sorts two of the standard's own named circumstances out of the terms and into planning
options.why: All three are on the same list and none of them is demoted to the strategy. Growth changes what is being audited and a misunderstanding changes what the client believes it is buying; the standard names both alongside the new reporting requirement precisely because each can make the existing terms describe something other than the engagement being performed.

options.text: No — a significant change in the nature or size of the entity's business, a change in other reporting requirements, and any indication that the entity misunderstands the objective and scope of the audit are each among the circumstances SA 210 names, and all three are present
options.why: The standard's list is wider than ownership, management and the framework. It also names a significant change in the nature or size of the entity's business, which one plant to nine plainly is; a change in other reporting requirements, which the sectoral regulator's new report is; and any indication that the entity misunderstands the objective and scope of the audit, which a request to confirm that the audit will detect any fraud by any employee is in one sentence.
keywords: nature or size of the entity's business

options.text: Yes on the facts, but the chief financial officer's letter should be answered in conversation, since a misunderstanding by one officer is not a change in the engagement
options.misconception: treats a stated misunderstanding of what the audit is for as a personal matter rather than as one of the circumstances the standard names
options.why: A conversation is worth having and is not the answer the standard gives. Any indication that the entity misunderstands the objective and scope of the audit is itself a listed circumstance, and the point of revising or reconfirming the terms is that the understanding ends up in writing rather than in somebody's memory of a call.

options.text: Yes — the circumstances the standard names are a change of senior management, a change in ownership and a change in the financial reporting framework, and none of the three has happened
options.misconception: treats the three best-known entries on the list as the whole of it
options.why: Those three are on the list and are not the list. The standard also reaches a change in the nature or size of the business, a change in legal or regulatory requirements, a change in other reporting requirements, revised or special terms, and any indication that the entity misunderstands the objective and scope of the audit.

citation.ref: para 13, read with the circumstances that may make it appropriate to revise the terms of the audit engagement or to remind the entity of the existing terms

items.scenario: Seventh year of the same audit. The owners are unchanged, the directors are unchanged and the financial reporting framework is unchanged. In the year the company went from one plant to nine and began operating in two new states; a sectoral regulator now requires an additional report from the statutory auditor each year; and the newly appointed chief financial officer has written asking you to confirm "that your audit will detect any fraud committed by any employee". The partner says none of the circumstances SA 210 lists has occurred.

items.stem: What does SA 300 say about who does the planning?

options.text: Nothing — planning is a manager's task, and the engagement partner discharges his responsibility by reviewing and approving the completed strategy and plan
options.misconception: satisfies a requirement to be involved in making the plan with an act performed after it is made
options.why: Approval at the end and involvement throughout are different things, and the standard asks for the second. A partner reading a finished plan can see what it says; he cannot see the alternatives that were never written down, which is where his experience would have been worth most.

options.text: Only the team discussion is a problem, and it is SA 315's requirement rather than SA 300's, so nothing in SA 300 has been breached
options.misconception: files the discussion under one standard alone, when SA 300 names participation in it as part of the involvement it requires
options.why: SA 315 has its own discussion requirement and that does not empty SA 300's. SA 300 names planning and participating in the discussion among engagement team members as part of what the engagement partner and other key members are to be involved in, so the seniors holding it alone fails both standards rather than only one.
keywords: planning and participating in the discussion
engagement partner and other key members

options.text: The engagement partner and other key members of the engagement team shall be involved in planning the audit, including participating in the discussion among engagement team members — their experience is what the involvement is for, and reviewing a finished plan is not being involved in making it
options.why: SA 300 states it as a requirement, not a preference: the engagement partner and other key members of the engagement team shall be involved in planning the audit, including planning and participating in the discussion among engagement team members. The reason the standard gives is that their involvement draws on their experience and insight, which enhances the effectiveness and efficiency of the planning process — and experience brought to a finished document can only approve or reject it, never shape where the work was aimed.
keywords: engagement partner and other key members

options.text: The engagement partner must perform the planning himself, since planning is the exercise of the judgement the opinion rests on and cannot be delegated
options.misconception: reads a requirement to be involved as a bar on anyone else doing the work
options.why: The standard requires involvement, not sole authorship, and it expressly contemplates other key members of the engagement team being involved alongside the partner. A manager and seniors drafting is normal; the partner absent from the drafting is what fails.
keywords: other key members of the engagement team

citation.ref: the requirement that the engagement partner and other key members of the engagement team be involved in planning the audit, including planning and participating in the discussion among engagement team members

items.scenario: On a large audit the manager and two seniors build the overall audit strategy and the audit plan over a fortnight. The engagement partner is committed to another client throughout and sees the plan for the first time when it is finished, reviewing it in an hour and signing it off. The discussion among the team about where the financial statements are most likely to be misstated is held by the two seniors between themselves.

items.stem: May the engagement partner date the auditor's report today?

options.text: No — the engagement partner has to satisfy himself, before he puts a date on the report, that the evidence on the file is both sufficient and appropriate: enough to carry the conclusions the team has come to, and enough for the report to go out. A finished engagement quality review does not supply evidence that has not yet arrived
options.why: SA 220 (Revised) sets two things before the date and the manager has counted only one. The first is the partner's own finding that sufficient appropriate audit evidence has been obtained — enough to stand behind the conclusions reached, and enough for the auditor's report to be issued. The second is quite separate: where an engagement quality review is required, no date may go on the report until he has been told the review is finished. A reviewer confirms that the judgements made were appropriate on what was on the file; he cannot confirm a confirmation that has not come back.
keywords: sufficient appropriate audit evidence has been obtained
for the auditor's report to be issued

options.text: No, and the answer is to date the report today with an Other Matter paragraph recording that two areas were still open at the date of signature
options.misconception: uses a paragraph in the report to disclose a shortage of evidence instead of obtaining the evidence
options.why: Describing a hole is not filling it. An Other Matter paragraph communicates something relevant to users' understanding of the audit; it cannot sit under an unmodified opinion that the partner is not yet in a position to support.

options.text: Yes, provided the report is dual dated next week when the confirmation and the actuary's letter arrive
options.misconception: borrows a mechanism built for facts arising after the report date and uses it to date a report before the evidence exists
options.why: Dual dating exists for a subsequent event amended after the original report was properly issued on complete evidence. It is not a way of issuing a report on incomplete evidence and finishing the audit afterwards; the original date would still be asserting that the evidence supporting the opinion was there when it was not.

options.text: Yes — the engagement quality review is complete and the manager's review is complete, which are the two requirements that gate the date
options.misconception: counts two reviews as the two gates, when one of the gates is about evidence rather than about review
options.why: The manager's review is not a gate on the date at all, and putting it in the pair hides the one that is missing. What gates the date alongside the engagement quality review is the engagement partner's own determination that sufficient appropriate audit evidence has been obtained.
keywords: not a gate on the date
sufficient appropriate audit evidence has been obtained

citation.ref: what the engagement partner must settle before a date goes on the report — that the evidence gathered is sufficient and appropriate, both to carry the conclusions and to let the report go out — read with the bar on dating it before he has been told that a required engagement quality review has finished

items.scenario: The engagement quality reviewer has finished and the engagement partner has been notified of it in writing. The manager has completed his review of every working paper. Two areas remain marked in the file as "conclusion pending — awaiting the confirmation from the counterparty and the actuary's final letter, both expected next week", one being a related party transaction and the other a warranty provision. The client wants the report dated today for a lender's deadline, and the manager says the two gates on the date have both been passed.

items.stem: How does SA 265 have you decide what goes to those charged with governance?

options.text: The cash finding goes up, but the two purchase-cycle findings stay out, neither being significant on its own
options.misconception: assesses deficiencies one at a time when the standard asks for them to be assessed individually or in combination
options.why: Assessing them one at a time is exactly what the standard rules out: deficiencies are judged individually or in combination. Two harmless findings that together let a buyer raise and approve his own order are a combination, and the combination is what is judged.

options.text: Deficiencies are assessed individually or in combination, on the likelihood that a misstatement could occur and on its potential magnitude — so a significant deficiency can exist even though no misstatement was identified during the audit, and the susceptibility to loss of an asset is one of the factors
options.why: What makes a deficiency significant is not whether something has already gone wrong. Two other things decide it: the likelihood that a misstatement could occur, and — should one occur — its potential magnitude. A deficiency can therefore be significant in a year where the audit turned up no misstatement at all, and susceptibility to loss of an asset counts in the weighing too. That reaches the cash finding directly, and it reaches the two purchase-cycle findings because the standard has deficiencies weighed individually or in combination.
keywords: likelihood that a misstatement could occur

options.text: Communicate nothing to those charged with governance — no misstatement was found, so no deficiency has been shown to be significant
options.misconception: makes an actual misstatement the test of significance, when the standard tests the likelihood of one and its potential size
options.why: A control that has not yet failed is not a control that works. A deficiency can be significant in a year when nothing at all was found to be misstated, which is the whole reason the test is written around likelihood and potential magnitude rather than around outcomes.

options.text: All three go up, since any deficiency touching cash or purchases is significant by nature and the late report is a deficiency too
options.misconception: replaces a judgement about likelihood and magnitude with a list of sensitive cycles, so a two-day reporting delay travels to the board
options.why: The cycle a deficiency sits in is not the test. Susceptibility to loss of an asset is one factor among several, and a report arriving two days late carries neither a real likelihood of misstatement nor a potential magnitude that would merit the attention of those charged with governance.

citation.ref: the determination of whether identified deficiencies, individually or in combination, constitute significant deficiencies, read with the significance of a deficiency depending on the likelihood and potential magnitude of misstatement and on susceptibility to loss of an asset

items.scenario: Three findings sit on the internal control memorandum. One person holds the cash and the cheque books and also performs the bank reconciliation; your testing found no misstatement in the cash cycle all year. In the purchase cycle, two smaller findings — a stale approval matrix and an unrestricted "urgent order" route — are each harmless alone, but together let one buyer raise and approve his own purchase order. A third finding is a monthly report that reaches the accounts team two days late. The senior proposes to communicate nothing to those charged with governance because no misstatement was found anywhere.

items.stem: What is wrong with that proposal?

options.text: The route the manager has chosen is not open to him — substantive procedures combined with tests of controls for the intervening period is available where the auditor relies on those controls, and none were tested here, so the remaining period has to be covered by further substantive procedures that themselves provide a reasonable basis for extending the audit conclusions from the interim date to the period end
options.why: SA 330 offers two routes across the gap, and they are not interchangeable on any facts. The first combines substantive procedures with tests of controls for the intervening period, which presupposes controls the auditor has tested and is relying on; a team that tested none all year cannot start relying on them for four months at the end. That leaves the second — further substantive procedures only, where the auditor determines that is sufficient — and whichever route is taken it must provide a reasonable basis for extending the audit conclusions from the interim date to the period end.
keywords: tests of controls for the intervening period
reasonable basis for extending the audit conclusions

options.text: Nothing, provided the tests of controls cover the whole of December to March rather than a sample of months within it
options.misconception: fixes the coverage of a procedure that cannot supply the evidence needed in the first place
options.why: Full coverage of the wrong evidence is still the wrong evidence. Controls that were never tested for design, implementation or operation over the first eight months give the auditor no basis for concluding they operated in the last four, however completely the last four are examined.

options.text: Nothing — the standard names two routes and leaves the choice between them to the auditor's judgement
options.misconception: reads two permitted routes as two routes always available, when the first depends on controls the auditor has actually tested
options.why: There is a choice, and it is a choice between routes that are open. The first route is built on tests of controls for the intervening period, so it exists only where there are controls being relied on; where the approach was wholly substantive from the start, the judgement is about the extent of the further substantive procedures, not about which route to take.
keywords: tests of controls for the intervening period

options.text: Nothing about the procedures, but a written representation from management that no material inventory movement occurred between 30 November and 31 March must be obtained as well
options.misconception: adds a representation to close a gap that only audit procedures can close
options.why: A written representation is audit evidence and is not sufficient appropriate audit evidence on its own about any of the matters it deals with. It cannot be the reasonable basis for extending the audit conclusions from the interim date to the period end, and obtaining one does not make the chosen route available.
keywords: reasonable basis for extending the audit conclusions

citation.ref: para 22 — covering the remaining period by substantive procedures combined with tests of controls for the intervening period, or by further substantive procedures alone, either providing a reasonable basis for extending the audit conclusions from the interim date to the period end

items.scenario: Inventory was substantively tested at 30 November for a 31 March year end and the results were clean. The team assessed a wholly substantive approach for inventory at the planning stage and tested no controls over inventory movements at any point in the year. The manager now proposes to cover December to March by performing tests of controls over goods received and goods despatched for that intervening period, and to do no further substantive work on inventory.

items.stem: What follows for the audit?

options.text: The control objective the review was necessary to achieve cannot be treated as achieved for this client, so the type 2 report supports no reliance on the accuracy of billed amounts, and the evidence over that has to come from your own substantive procedures
options.why: A complementary user entity control is one the service organisation assumed, in designing its service, that user entities would implement, and it is named in the description because the stated control objective cannot be achieved without it. The service auditor never tests it, and his unmodified opinion says nothing about it. Where the user entity has not implemented it, the chain the control objective depends on is broken at the client's end, and the auditor obtains the evidence he needs by his own substantive procedures instead.

options.text: Nothing follows for reliance — the report is unmodified and covers the whole year, so the unimplemented review is a matter for the management letter
options.misconception: reads an unmodified service auditor's opinion as covering a control that was never inside its scope
options.why: The opinion covers the provider's controls and only those. The description names the review precisely because the provider does not perform it, so an unmodified opinion is exactly what you would expect to see whether or not the client ever did.

options.text: Report the failure to the provider, which will extend its own controls to cover the rate table review from next month
options.misconception: hands back to the service organisation a control it deliberately left with the user entity, and treats a future fix as evidence about the year under audit
options.why: The provider designed its service on the footing that somebody at the client would look at the rate table, which is why it is a complementary user entity control rather than one of the provider's own. And a control extended next month says nothing about the twelve months being audited.

options.text: The service auditor's opinion must be treated as modified, a complementary user entity control that was not implemented having invalidated his report
options.misconception: makes a failure at the user entity a defect in a report about a different entity
options.why: Nothing about the provider's system has changed. The report remains a correct statement about the provider; what has failed is at the client, and it is the user auditor's reliance on the report, not the report itself, that the failure destroys.

citation.ref: para 8(a) and the requirement, when a type 1 or type 2 report is used, to determine whether the complementary user entity controls identified by the service organisation are relevant and to test them at the user entity
