items.stem: What may you do?

options.text: Withdraw only after issuing the audit report for the full year, because the directive the Securities and Exchange Board of India has issued about an auditor stepping down leaves no room to walk away from the engagement with no report behind you — so in practice the report is issued, and on these facts it disclaims an opinion
options.why: SA 705 (Revised) puts withdrawal first only where withdrawal is practicable and possible under applicable law or regulation, and disclaims where it is not. For a listed company that second branch is the live one. Two things bind him — the terms on which the company is listed, and what the securities regulator has laid down about an auditor stepping down — and together they do not permit withdrawing from the engagement without issuing a report for the period. Where limited review reports have gone out for all three quarters, he issues the audit report for the full year and resigns after that. What the report carries on these facts is a disclaimer of opinion.
keywords: practicable and possible under applicable law or regulation
do not permit withdrawing from the engagement without issuing
the audit report for the full year

options.text: Resign now and say in the resignation letter that the reason is professional pre-occupation, leaving the incoming auditor to deal with the division
options.misconception: reaches for a form of words the Institute has expressly told auditors not to use, on top of a resignation the securities regulator does not permit
options.why: Two things are wrong with it. The resignation itself is not permitted without the report. And the Institute has announced that an auditor of an unlisted company shall not give professional pre-occupation as the reason for resignation and shall state the reasons clearly in the resignation letter, so the sentence proposed here is the one form of words that has been ruled out.

options.text: Issue the audit report with a qualified opinion, since resigning is barred and a disclaimer would be too severe for a single division
options.misconception: lowers the modification because the exit is blocked, when the blocked exit changes only who reports and not what the report says
options.why: The regulator's rule decides whether he may leave, not what his opinion is. The opinion still follows from the conclusion he has reached — possible effects of undetected misstatements that could be both material and pervasive — and that conclusion gives a disclaimer.

options.text: Resign at once without any further report, since the standard directs withdrawal wherever the possible effects could be material and pervasive
options.misconception: reads the withdrawal branch as unconditional, dropping the words that make it conditional on law and regulation
options.why: The direction is conditional on its face. The auditor withdraws where withdrawal is practicable and possible under applicable law or regulation, and disclaims an opinion where withdrawal before issuing the report is not practicable or possible. A rule of the securities regulator that forbids resigning without a report is exactly what makes it not possible.

citation.ref: Ch. Reporting — where the auditor's withdrawal is not permitted, the Securities and Exchange Board of India circular of 18 October 2019 on the resignation of an auditor and the requirement to issue the audit or limited review report before resigning, read with SA 705 (Revised) para 13 and para 14

items.scenario: You are the statutory auditor of a listed company. Halfway through the audit of the year ended 31 March, management refuses you access to the records of a division that carries a large part of the company's revenue, and refuses again after you ask for the limitation to be removed. You communicate the refusal to the audit committee. No alternative procedure gets you to the revenue of that division, and you conclude that the possible effects of undetected misstatements could be both material and pervasive. You have already issued limited review reports for all three quarters of the year. Your partner reads SA 705 (Revised), sees that withdrawal comes before a disclaimer, and proposes to resign from the engagement at once without issuing anything further.

items.stem: What else does SA 705 (Revised) require him to change or remove?

options.text: The sentence saying the financial statements have been audited becomes one saying he was engaged to audit them; the pointer to the section describing his responsibilities goes, and so does the sentence about the evidence being enough to found an opinion; and the responsibilities description shrinks to three sentences — that his job was to run an audit under the Standards on Auditing and to report, that the matters set out under the Basis for Disclaimer of Opinion heading left him without evidence enough to found an opinion on, and the sentence about independence and other ethical responsibilities
options.why: A disclaimer changes the report in more places than the two headings. Where SA 700 has the financial statements being audited, the sentence is amended to say the auditor was engaged to audit them. Two SA 700 elements drop out entirely — a reference to the section where the auditor's responsibilities are described, and the sentence asking whether what he gathered was sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for the opinion, which on a disclaimer would say the opposite of what the rest of the report says. And his responsibilities description is amended to include only those three statements.
keywords: reference to the section where the auditor's responsibilities are described
sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for the opinion

options.text: Only the description of the auditor's responsibilities, which is shortened; the sentence about the sufficiency of the audit evidence stays, because it describes what he did rather than what he concluded
options.misconception: keeps the evidence sentence by reading it as a description of work done, when it is a statement that the evidence provides a basis for an opinion the auditor is not expressing
options.why: That sentence does not report effort. It states that what the auditor gathered was enough, and apt, to provide a basis for the auditor's opinion, which is the exact proposition a disclaimer denies, and SA 705 (Revised) directs that a report disclaiming an opinion shall not include it.
keywords: provide a basis for the auditor's opinion

options.text: The whole auditor's responsibilities section is removed, since an auditor who expresses no opinion has no responsibilities to describe
options.misconception: deletes a section the standard reduces, and denies responsibilities that the auditor plainly still carries
options.why: The section is amended, not deleted. It keeps three statements, and one of them exists to say what his responsibility was — to conduct an audit in accordance with the Standards on Auditing and to issue an auditor's report. The independence statement stays as well.

options.text: Nothing else. The Opinion and Basis sections carry the modification and the rest of the report is standard wording that the standard does not touch
options.misconception: treats the modification as confined to the two sections that carry the opinion, when a disclaimer reaches into the responsibilities description and the evidence statement as well
options.why: Leaving the standard wording in place produces a report that disclaims an opinion in one section and asserts in another that the evidence obtained was sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for that opinion. The standard removes the second statement precisely because it contradicts the first.
keywords: disclaims an opinion in one section

citation.ref: the requirement on a disclaimer to state that the auditor does not express an opinion and that because of the significance of the matters described he has not been able to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence, to amend the SA 700 (Revised) statement that the financial statements have been audited to say that the auditor was engaged to audit them, to omit the reference to the section describing the auditor's responsibilities and the statement about the sufficiency of the audit evidence, and to amend the description of the auditor's responsibilities to include only the three statements named, read with para 16

items.scenario: An audit senior is preparing a report that will disclaim an opinion because of an inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence. He has changed the Opinion heading and the Basis heading, and has written the two required sentences in the Opinion section. He has then left the rest of the standard report exactly as it stands for an unmodified opinion — the whole of the section setting out what he was responsible for, the cross-reference pointing to it, and the sentence saying that what he gathered was enough, and apt, to found an opinion on.

items.stem: What does SA 705 (Revised) require?

options.text: Both remaining matters are described in the Basis for Adverse Opinion section, with the reasons and their effects, and the sentence about the sufficiency of the audit evidence is amended to include the word "adverse"
options.why: The standard says it in terms. An adverse opinion, or a disclaimer, does not close the Basis for Opinion section: the auditor still sets out there why any other matters of which he is aware would themselves have called for a modification, and the effects thereof. Separately, on a qualified or an adverse opinion, the sentence asking whether what he gathered was enough, and apt, to found the opinion is amended to include the word "qualified" or "adverse" as appropriate.
keywords: any other matters of which he is aware

options.text: The other two matters are left out, because an adverse opinion is the most severe conclusion on a misstatement and already covers everything else
options.misconception: treats the severity of the opinion as absorbing every other matter, when the standard requires each one to be described whatever the opinion says
options.why: Severity is not coverage. A reader of a report with an adverse opinion still needs to know what else was wrong and by how much, which is why the requirement to describe other matters that would have required a modification applies even after an adverse opinion or a disclaimer.

options.text: Only the depreciation matter is described, because it is a known misstatement; the missing confirmations concern evidence, and evidence matters are reported only where they drive the opinion
options.misconception: limits the requirement to known misstatements, when the requirement is about any matter that would have required a modification, from either row of the matrix
options.why: An inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence is one of the two things that require a modification, so a matter of that kind is one that would have required a modification. Where the modification results from an inability to obtain evidence, the Basis for Opinion section carries the reasons for that inability.
keywords: one of the two things that require a modification

options.text: Both matters are described, but the sentence about the sufficiency of the audit evidence is removed altogether, as it is on a disclaimer
options.misconception: applies the disclaimer's removal of that sentence to an adverse opinion, where the standard amends the sentence instead of dropping it
options.why: Removing it is what a disclaimer does. On a qualified or an adverse opinion the auditor has obtained the evidence and reached a conclusion, so the sentence stays and is amended to include the word "qualified" or "adverse" as appropriate.
keywords: Removing it is what a disclaimer does
the sentence stays and is amended

citation.ref: the requirement that the sentence about the sufficiency of the evidence pick up the word "qualified" or "adverse", and the requirement that an adverse opinion or a disclaimer does not excuse the auditor from setting out in the Basis for Opinion section why every other matter he knows of would itself have called for a modification, and what its effects are, read with para 20 and para 21

items.scenario: You are signing a report with an adverse opinion, because the company has consolidated a subsidiary it does not control and the effects run through every primary statement. Two other matters remain unresolved. Depreciation on a class of plant has been charged on a basis that you consider wrong, by an amount that would on its own have been material but not pervasive. And you were unable to obtain confirmations for a block of trade receivables, again material but not pervasive on its own. Your manager's view is that once the opinion is adverse the other two matters are absorbed by it and adding them would only confuse the reader. He also proposes to leave the sentence about the sufficiency of the audit evidence exactly as the unmodified template has it.

items.stem: What goes into the Basis for Qualified Opinion section?

options.text: An explanation of how the disclosure is misstated — what the note says, what the applicable framework requires it to say, and in what respect the two differ
options.why: Where a material misstatement relates to narrative disclosures, what the Basis for Opinion section has to carry is an explanation of how the disclosures are misstated. Sizing the financial effect is what the standard asks for on a misstatement of specific amounts, and nothing here moves an amount, so the section carries the explanation rather than a figure.
keywords: an explanation of how the disclosures are misstated

options.text: A description and quantification of the financial effects of the misstatement, or a statement that quantification is impracticable
options.misconception: applies the rule for a misstatement of specific amounts to a misstatement that is entirely narrative
options.why: That rule is for a misstatement of specific amounts — figures carried on the face of the statements, and the numbers set out in the notes beside them. A narrative disclosure has its own rule, which asks for an explanation of how it is misstated rather than for a number or an excuse for the absence of one.

options.text: Nothing. The Basis section names the matter and the note, and the reader can compare the note with the framework for himself
options.misconception: reduces the Basis section to a cross-reference, which is the one thing the standard says does not amount to a qualification
options.why: The Basis for Opinion section must include a description of the matter giving rise to the modification, stated from the auditor's standpoint. A pointer to management's note leaves the reader with management's account of the matter and none of the auditor's.
keywords: a description of the matter giving rise to the modification

options.text: The disclosure the company should have made, written out by the auditor in full
options.misconception: reaches for the remedy that belongs to an omitted disclosure and applies it to one that exists but is wrong
options.why: Including the omitted disclosures is what the auditor does where the misstatement is a non-disclosure of information required to be disclosed, and even then only where it is not prohibited by law or regulation, it is practicable, and he has obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence about the omitted information. Here a disclosure exists and is inadequate, which is the narrative limb.
keywords: non-disclosure of information required to be disclosed

citation.ref: the requirement that where the wording of a disclosure is what is materially misstated, the Basis for Opinion section explain in what respect it misstates the position, distinguished from the requirement in para 21 that applies where the misstatement is of specific amounts

items.scenario: A company has been served with a demand from a regulator that could, on the company's own counsel's assessment, cost it a sum larger than a year's profit. The company treats it as a contingent liability, which you accept, but the note in the financial statements gives only the name of the regulator and the words "the matter is under appeal". It gives no estimate of the financial effect, no indication of the uncertainties, and no statement that an estimate cannot be made. Management will not expand the note. You conclude that the disclosure is materially misstated but that the effect is not pervasive. No amount in the balance sheet or the statement of profit and loss changes as a result.

items.stem: What does SA 705 (Revised) require you to do about the omitted disclosure?

options.text: Discuss the non-disclosure with those charged with governance, describe in the Basis for Qualified Opinion section the nature of the omitted information, and include the omitted disclosures themselves in that section
options.why: Where a material misstatement is the non-disclosure of information required to be disclosed, the standard sets three steps. First the auditor discusses the non-disclosure with those charged with governance. Then the Basis for Opinion section is made to say what kind of thing is missing — the nature of the omitted information. Last, and unless prohibited by law or regulation, the absent disclosure goes into that section itself, provided doing so is practicable and the auditor already holds the evidence he needs about what was left out — all three conditions are met on these facts.
keywords: discusses the non-disclosure with those charged with governance
the nature of the omitted information
unless prohibited by law or regulation

options.text: Include the omitted disclosures only if management first agrees, since a disclosure the company has not made is management's information to publish
options.misconception: makes an auditor's reporting duty conditional on the consent of the party whose omission caused it
options.why: The conditions the standard attaches are three: that inclusion is not prohibited by law or regulation, that it can practicably be done, and that the auditor already holds the evidence he needs about what was left out. Management's agreement is not among them, and a rule that needed it would never operate.
keywords: not prohibited by law or regulation
Management's agreement is not among them

options.text: Report the matter as a key audit matter instead, since it is a matter of most significance that you communicated to those charged with governance
options.misconception: moves a matter that requires a modification into the key audit matters section, which the standards say is not a substitute for one
options.why: Communicating key audit matters is not a substitute for the auditor expressing a modified opinion when the circumstances require it. A material non-disclosure that management will not correct requires a modification, and the key audit matters section cannot carry it.
keywords: not a substitute for the auditor expressing a modified opinion

options.text: Describe the nature of the omitted information, but do not reproduce the disclosure — putting management's disclosure into the auditor's report would make the auditor the preparer of the financial statements
options.misconception: refuses a step the standard requires, on a principle the standard has already weighed and answered
options.why: The standard expressly directs the auditor to include the omitted disclosures, subject to three conditions, and reproducing them in the Basis for Opinion section does not put them into the financial statements. Management remains the preparer; the auditor is reporting what should have been there.
keywords: expressly directs the auditor to include the omitted disclosures

citation.ref: the three steps that follow where what is materially misstated is a disclosure the framework demanded and the company left out — the omission raised with those charged with governance, the Basis for Opinion section naming what kind of thing is missing, and the absent disclosure set out there in full where the law permits it, where it can practicably be done, and where the evidence about what was left out is already held

items.scenario: A company's financial statements omit a disclosure that the applicable financial reporting framework requires: the terms and the ageing of amounts owed to a group of related parties. You have the underlying records, you have tested them, and you can set the disclosure out yourself. Management declines to add it, saying the information is commercially sensitive. Nothing in any law or regulation prevents the information being published. You conclude that the non-disclosure is material but not pervasive.

items.stem: How is pervasiveness tested here?

options.text: It cannot be met. Pervasiveness measures the spread of a misstatement across the primary statements, and a defect in one note has no spread
options.misconception: keeps only the first two limbs of the definition and drops the one the standard added for disclosures
options.why: The definition has three limbs, and the third is expressly about disclosures. Reading the test as a measure of spread across the primary statements makes a whole class of misstatements incapable of ever being pervasive, which is not what the standard says.

options.text: By the third limb of the definition — in relation to disclosures, whether the effects are fundamental to users' understanding of the financial statements — so an inadequate disclosure can be pervasive even though no amount moves, and the answer turns on how far short the note falls
options.why: Pervasive effects come in three kinds. They may be not confined to specific elements, accounts or items at all. They may be so confined and still stand for a substantial proportion of what the statements report. Or, where the fault lies in disclosure, they may be fundamental to users' understanding of the position. The third limb is written for disclosures and asks nothing about amounts. A note that is incomplete gives a qualified opinion where the effect is material but not pervasive; a material uncertainty left out altogether is fundamental to users' understanding and gives an adverse opinion.

options.text: By whether the going concern basis is still appropriate. It is, so the statements are not materially misstated and no modification arises
options.misconception: confuses the appropriateness of the basis of accounting with the adequacy of the disclosure about the uncertainty
options.why: Two separate questions. The basis of accounting can be appropriate and the financial statements still be materially misstated because the material uncertainty attaching to it is not adequately disclosed. That inadequate disclosure is the misstatement.

options.text: By whether the matter was communicated to those charged with governance and determined to be a key audit matter; if it was, an emphasis of matter paragraph resolves it
options.misconception: routes an uncorrected misstatement through the reporting choices that exist only where no modification is required
options.why: An emphasis of matter paragraph is available only where the auditor would not be required to modify the opinion as a result of the matter, and only for a matter appropriately presented or disclosed. A material uncertainty that is not adequately disclosed is neither.
keywords: would not be required to modify the opinion

citation.ref: para 5 on the three limbs of pervasiveness, the third of which reaches a defect in disclosure so central that a reader could not understand the position without it, read with para 7(a) and para 8 on the choice between a qualified and an adverse opinion where a material uncertainty is inadequately disclosed

items.scenario: A company's financing arrangements have expired and it has not been able to renegotiate them or find replacement finance. You conclude that a material uncertainty exists that may cast significant doubt on its ability to continue as a going concern. The notes describe the size of the facilities and the date they expired, but say nothing at all about the effect of the failure to refinance or about the availability of refinancing, so the material uncertainty is not adequately disclosed. Every figure in the balance sheet and the statement of profit and loss has been prepared on the going concern basis, which you accept as appropriate. The company will not add to the note. A colleague argues that since no amount is misstated and the disclosure defect touches only one note, the pervasiveness test cannot be met and the most that is available is a qualified opinion.

items.stem: What does SA 705 (Revised) allow you to do?

options.text: Express an adverse opinion, because the combined effect could be large enough that the accounts, read as a whole, cease to give a true and fair view
options.misconception: converts an inability to form any opinion into a positive opinion that the statements are wrong
options.why: An adverse opinion is a conclusion, reached on sufficient appropriate audit evidence, that misstatements are both material and pervasive. Nothing here says the statements are misstated. The auditor's difficulty is that he cannot say whether they are.

options.text: Express an unmodified opinion with an emphasis of matter paragraph for each of the four matters, since each is properly disclosed and you have the evidence on each
options.misconception: answers the four uncertainties one at a time, which is exactly the reading the multiple-uncertainties provision exists to displace
options.why: Taken one at a time that would be right, and it is why the provision is worded around the interaction of the uncertainties rather than around any of them alone. Where the auditor concludes he cannot form an opinion because of what the combination might do, an unmodified opinion is not available whatever the individual paragraphs say. A widespread use of emphasis of matter paragraphs also diminishes the effectiveness of the communication.

options.text: Qualify the opinion, since each uncertainty on its own is material but not pervasive
options.misconception: adds the individual assessments together arithmetically, when the standard's concern is the interaction between them rather than their sum
options.why: The provision is not about accumulating four material items. It is about the potential interaction of the uncertainties and their possible cumulative effect, which is what makes the outcome unstateable rather than merely large.

options.text: Disclaim an opinion, on the footing that in extremely rare circumstances involving multiple uncertainties the auditor may conclude that, notwithstanding having obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence regarding each individual uncertainty, it is not possible to form an opinion because of the potential interaction of the uncertainties and their possible cumulative effect
options.why: There are two routes to a disclaimer and this is the second one. It does not depend on evidence being missing — the standard's own words are notwithstanding having obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence on every uncertainty taken by itself — but on the potential interaction between them and on their possible cumulative effect, which together make an opinion impossible to form. Four open matters whose outcomes change each other's meaning is the case it describes.
keywords: notwithstanding having obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence

citation.ref: the ground for disclaiming in extremely rare circumstances where several uncertainties are open at once — evidence held on each of them taken by itself, and no opinion formable even so, because of how they may act on one another and what they may come to in total

items.scenario: You are auditing a construction company for the year ended 31 March. Four things are open at once. A tax authority has raised a demand that the company is contesting, and its counsel puts the outcome at genuinely uncertain. A joint venture partner has begun arbitration seeking to unwind a contract that carries most of the order book, and the tribunal has not been constituted. The company's principal lender has served a notice of default and has not said whether it will call the loan. And a state government has issued a show cause notice that could cancel the licence for the company's largest project. You have obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence about each of the four separately — the demand, the pleadings, the notice and the show cause notice are all on your file, and management's disclosures about each are complete and properly presented. What you cannot do is say what the four come to together: the outcome of any one of them changes what the others mean, and the combinations run from no effect at all to the company ceasing to exist.

items.stem: Which describes the two routes to a disclaimer correctly?

options.text: The second route is a disclaimer given where management has imposed a limitation on scope and withdrawal is not practicable
options.misconception: names a third situation that is really the first route reached by a particular path, and mistakes it for the multiple-uncertainties provision
options.why: That is the first route arrived at through a management-imposed limitation: the auditor is still unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence, and the possible effects could be both material and pervasive. Evidence is missing there, which is what separates it from the multiple-uncertainties case.
keywords: unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence

options.text: The second route applies whenever there is more than one going concern indicator, so that two or more indicators together always give a disclaimer
options.misconception: turns a rare judgement into a counting rule, and attaches it to one topic the standard does not name
options.why: The provision is not tied to going concern and does not count anything. It applies in extremely rare circumstances, and only where the auditor concludes that the potential interaction of the uncertainties and their possible cumulative effect make it impossible to form an opinion.

options.text: Only one route exists. Every disclaimer follows from an inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence, and a matter about which the auditor has evidence can never produce one
options.misconception: knows the common route and treats it as the only one, which leaves the multiple-uncertainties provision with nothing to do
options.why: If that were so the standard would not separately provide for the case where the auditor has obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence regarding each of the individual uncertainties and still cannot form an opinion. The provision exists and is worded to make exactly that point.

options.text: One route is an inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence where the possible effects of undetected misstatements could be both material and pervasive; the other needs no missing evidence at all and rests on the auditor being unable to form an opinion because of the potential interaction of multiple uncertainties, in extremely rare circumstances
options.why: Both are in the standard. The first is the familiar one and sits on the second row of the matrix. The second is separate and expressly assumes the evidence was obtained regarding each of the individual uncertainties, the difficulty being their potential interaction and possible cumulative effect. The words extremely rare are the standard's own and mark it as the exception rather than an easier way out of a hard judgement.

citation.ref: the two circumstances in which the auditor shall disclaim an opinion — an inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence where the possible effects of undetected misstatements could be both material and pervasive, and extremely rare circumstances involving multiple uncertainties where notwithstanding sufficient appropriate audit evidence on each it is not possible to form an opinion

items.scenario: Two audit assistants are arguing about when a disclaimer of opinion may be given. One says a disclaimer always means the auditor did not get the evidence he needed. The other says he has read of a disclaimer where the auditor had all the evidence.

items.stem: What does the auditor do?

options.text: Modify the opinion, expressing it as "except for" the effects of the matter, and state the qualification independently in the report from the auditor's own standpoint, whatever the note says
options.why: The note is management's stand on the matter; the qualification is the auditor's record of his disagreement, and disclosure by management does not discharge him. Where notes of a qualificatory nature appear, all qualifications are stated independently in the report so that a reader can weigh them, and the report must state the matter from the auditor's standpoint and not from management's. The qualification is expressed in a clear and unambiguous manner as "except for" the effects of the matter to which it relates.

options.text: Give the opinion "subject to" the note, which records the disagreement while acknowledging that management has disclosed the facts
options.misconception: accepts a form of words the study material rules out precisely because it is not forceful enough to be read as a qualification
options.why: Phrases such as "subject to" and "with the foregoing explanation" are not sufficiently clear or forceful and are not appropriate in the opinion paragraph. A qualified opinion is expressed as "except for" the effects of the matter to which the qualification relates.

options.text: Leave the opinion unmodified and refer in the report to management's note, since a reference to a note of a qualificatory nature operates as a qualification
options.misconception: treats a cross-reference as doing the work of a qualification, which is the confusion the rule was written to stop
options.why: A reference to the notes to accounts in the auditor's report does not automatically become a qualification. It carries management's account of the matter into a report that is supposed to carry the auditor's.
keywords: does not automatically become a qualification

options.text: Leave the opinion unmodified and add an emphasis of matter paragraph drawing attention to the note, since the matter is now presented in the financial statements
options.misconception: uses an emphasis paragraph in place of a modification, which the standard forbids in terms
options.why: An emphasis of matter is open only where the matter is appropriately presented and the auditor already holds the evidence he needs about it. A misstatement management refuses to correct is not appropriately presented, and an emphasis of matter is not a substitute for a modification of the opinion.
keywords: not a substitute for a modification

citation.ref: Ch. Reporting — the distinction between notes on accounts and qualifications, the requirement that a qualification be expressed as "except for" in a clear and unambiguous manner, and the rule that a reference to a note does not automatically become a qualification

items.scenario: You have concluded that a company's inventory is overstated because obsolete lines have not been written down. Management disagrees with you on the facts but agrees to add a note setting out its own assessment of the position and recording that the auditors take a different view. The note is full and fair as an account of management's position, and it names the amount in dispute. The finance director then asks you to leave the opinion unmodified, on the footing that a reader now has everything he needs, and offers as a compromise that your report may say the opinion is given "subject to" the note.

items.stem: What is wrong with the report as drafted?

options.text: Nothing, provided the notes referred to are complete and accurate; the report and the financial statements are read together and duplication helps nobody
options.misconception: relies on the completeness of management's notes to supply the auditor's own statement, which no note can do
options.why: Completeness is not the test. The note is management's stand on the matter and the report has to state the matter from the auditor's standpoint; a reference to the notes does not automatically become a qualification however good the notes are.
keywords: does not automatically become a qualification

options.text: The three matters belong in an emphasis of matter section, since they are already disclosed in the notes
options.misconception: moves qualificatory matters into a paragraph reserved for matters that require no modification
options.why: An emphasis of matter paragraph is available only where the auditor would not be required to modify the opinion as a result of the matter. The partner has already accepted that these three are qualificatory in nature, which puts them outside it.
keywords: would not be required to modify the opinion

options.text: Three qualifications have not been stated at all. Where notes of a qualificatory nature appear in the accounts, the auditor states all his qualifications independently in his report, from his own standpoint, so that the reader can assess their significance
options.why: A qualification exists only when the auditor makes it. Where notes of a qualificatory nature appear in the accounts, he must state all qualifications independently in his report, and state them there so a reader can assess the significance each of them carries; every one of them has to be contained in the auditor's report itself. Three sentences pointing at three notes leave the reader with management's account of three matters and the auditor's account of none.
keywords: state all qualifications independently in his report

options.text: The opinion should have been adverse, because four qualificatory matters together are always pervasive
options.misconception: converts a count of matters into a pervasiveness conclusion, which is a judgement about effects and not about number
options.why: Pervasiveness is judged on whether the effects are confined to specific elements, whether if so confined they represent a substantial proportion of the financial statements, or whether in relation to disclosures they are fundamental to users' understanding. How many matters there are does not answer any of those.

citation.ref: Ch. Reporting — the notes and report relationship, the requirement that all qualifications be stated independently in the auditor's report and be contained in it, and the rule that a reference to a note does not automatically become a qualification

items.scenario: A draft auditor's report on a company runs to four pages. The opinion paragraph is qualified "except for" one matter, which is described in the Basis for Qualified Opinion section. Three further matters that the engagement partner accepts are qualificatory in nature have been dealt with by a single sentence at the end of the report reading that attention is drawn to notes 14, 19 and 23. The partner's reasoning is that the notes are complete, that repeating them would make the report unreadable, and that any reader who wants the detail can turn to the accounts.

items.stem: On what does the choice turn?

options.text: On whether the matter can be quantified. An unquantifiable matter cannot support a qualification and can only be emphasised
options.misconception: makes quantification the gate to a qualification, when the standard provides for a matter that cannot practicably be quantified
options.why: Where a misstatement relates to specific amounts the auditor describes and quantifies the financial effects unless it is impracticable, and where it is impracticable he says so in the Basis for Opinion section. Inability to quantify changes what the section says, not whether the opinion is modified.
keywords: not whether the opinion is modified

options.text: On whether management agrees to the paragraph. A matter fully disclosed by management and accepted as accurate by the auditor needs nothing further in the report
options.misconception: lets management's disclosure close a question the auditor is required to answer for himself
options.why: Client and auditor are separate parties and the auditor exercises his own professional judgement here. The whole point of the rule is that management's having disclosed the facts does not tell the auditor what his report should say.

options.text: On the auditor's own judgement about whether disclosure alone suffices — full disclosure by management does not settle it, and where an irregularity amounts to a breach of law the auditor brings it to the notice of the shareholders by properly qualifying his report
options.why: The study material puts the judgement on the auditor. Management may insist that it has disclosed the full facts, but the auditor assesses whether the disclosure alone would suffice or whether he must also modify his report or add an emphasis of matter. Where what the company did was an irregularity amounting to a breach of law, the shareholders are the people who have to be told, and he tells them by properly qualifying his report.
keywords: whether the disclosure alone would suffice

options.text: On whether the breach affects the current year. A breach whose consequences fall in a later year is a matter for the next auditor
options.misconception: defers a matter to a later period on the basis of when its cost lands, rather than when the irregularity occurred
options.why: The irregularity was committed during the year under audit and the auditor knows of it. That is what he reports on, and postponing it leaves the shareholders of this year's accounts uninformed about this year's breach.

citation.ref: Ch. Reporting — the auditor's professional judgement on whether disclosure alone suffices, the rule that an emphasis of matter is not a substitute for modification of the opinion, and the direction that a breach of law be brought to the notice of the shareholders by properly qualifying the report

items.scenario: A company has breached a statutory requirement during the year. The breach is not itself a misstatement of any amount, and the directors have disclosed it fully in a note that describes what happened, what it may cost and what the company has done since. The auditor is satisfied the note is accurate and has the evidence to support every sentence in it. He is deciding what, if anything, his report should say.

items.stem: What does SA 705 (Revised) require, and what has been missed?

options.text: Nothing has been missed. The standard requires the auditor to inform those charged with governance that the opinion will be modified, which the note to the audit committee chair did
options.misconception: stops at the fact of the modification, which is the half of the requirement that was met, and drops the wording
options.why: The requirement names two things and the wording of the modification is the second. A board told only that there will be a qualification, and first seeing the sentence in the signed report, has not been given what the standard asks for.

options.text: Where the auditor expects to modify the opinion he owes those charged with governance two things — the sentence his modification will take, and why he expects to modify at all — so the wording should have gone to the audit committee before the report was signed, and telling the chief financial officer is not telling those charged with governance
options.why: The requirement has two halves and only one of them was met. What goes across is the wording of the modification as well as the circumstances that led to the expected modification, and he is required to discuss and deliberate the audit findings and the type of misstatements with those charged with governance. Management is not those charged with governance, and a one-line note that a qualification is coming is not the wording of the modification.
keywords: the circumstances that led to the expected modification
Management is not those charged with governance

options.text: Nothing has been missed, because the communication was made to the chief financial officer, who is the officer responsible for the financial statements and will brief the board
options.misconception: substitutes a communication to management for one to those charged with governance, and relies on management to relay it
options.why: Communicating with management is a different requirement with a different purpose. The obligation here runs to those charged with governance, and it is not discharged by telling the person whose accounting the modification is about.

options.text: The communication should have waited until the report was signed, because sharing draft wording before signature exposes the auditor to pressure to change it
options.misconception: postpones a communication whose whole purpose is to happen while the matter can still be discussed
options.why: The trigger is the expectation of a modification, not the signature. The communication is made so that the circumstances can be discussed and deliberated with those charged with governance while something can still be done about them.

citation.ref: the requirement that an expected modification be put to those charged with governance in two parts — the sentence the auditor expects to write, and why he expects to write it — read with SA 260 (Revised) para 16

items.scenario: Ten days before the board meeting at which a company's accounts are to be approved, you decide that you will have to qualify your opinion over a revenue cut-off matter. You email the chief financial officer setting out the matter and the amount. On the morning of the board meeting you send the audit committee chair a one-line note saying that the report will carry a qualification. The drafted wording of the qualification is not shared with anybody outside the firm until the signed report is tabled.

items.stem: What effect does that have on the opinion?

options.text: The disagreement is itself reported, and the opinion becomes a disclaimer because the auditor and those charged with governance cannot agree on the facts
options.misconception: turns a disagreement about the accounting into an inability to obtain evidence, which is a different row of the matrix
options.why: A disclaimer is for an inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence, or for extremely rare interacting uncertainties. A disagreement about whether an amount is misstated, where the auditor has the evidence, gives a qualified or an adverse opinion depending on pervasiveness.
keywords: an inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence

options.text: The auditor must reconsider and, if the committee's view is reasonable, express an unmodified opinion, since those charged with governance are the body the standard requires him to satisfy
options.misconception: reads a communication duty as a duty to be satisfied by the recipient, which would put the opinion in the hands of the audited
options.why: Nothing in the requirement makes the modification conditional on the committee. An auditor who could be talked out of a modification by the body he reports to would not be expressing an independent opinion at all.

options.text: None. The communication is a requirement about telling and deliberating, not about obtaining agreement, and the opinion continues to follow from the auditor's own conclusion on the audit evidence
options.why: The requirement is that the auditor communicate the circumstances and the wording and discuss and deliberate the findings with those charged with governance. It is not a requirement to obtain their agreement, and their disagreement does not enter the decision. A modification follows once the auditor concludes either that the statements, taken in the round, are not free from material misstatement, or that the evidence he needs cannot be got.
keywords: not a requirement to obtain their agreement

options.text: The auditor may treat the communication requirement as met and issue the report without the modification, provided he records the committee's resolution in his working papers
options.misconception: lets documentation of the disagreement stand in for the modification the evidence requires
options.why: Documenting a disagreement records what happened; it does not change what the report must say. The modification follows from the auditor's conclusion on the audit evidence, and a minute cannot displace it.

citation.ref: the requirement to put an expected modification to those charged with governance in two parts — the sentence the auditor expects to write, and why he expects to write it — read with the two circumstances in which a modification is required at all: a conclusion that the statements, taken in the round, are not free from material misstatement, or evidence that cannot be got

items.scenario: An audit committee receives the auditor's communication of an expected adverse opinion, together with the proposed wording. It discusses the matter over two meetings, disagrees with the auditor's view, records its disagreement in the minutes, and resolves that in its judgement the financial statements are correct as drawn. It then writes to the auditor stating that, having considered the matter, it does not accept the modification and asking him to proceed on the basis that the communication requirement has been complied with and the outcome settled.

items.stem: Which of the four may be dealt with by an emphasis of matter paragraph?

options.text: Only the fire, because a subsequent event is the one circumstance the standard names for an emphasis of matter
options.misconception: keeps one item off the illustrative list and treats it as the whole of it
options.why: A significant subsequent event is one of four named circumstances, alongside an uncertainty about the outcome of exceptional litigation or regulatory action, early application of a new accounting standard, and a major catastrophe. The list is illustrative rather than exhaustive in either direction.

options.text: All four, since each is important enough that a reader would want to know about it
options.misconception: reads the paragraph as a place for anything important, dropping the requirement that the matter be in the financial statements
options.why: Importance is only half the test. The paragraph attaches to something already appropriately presented or disclosed in the financial statements, and it may point at nothing else. The state of the internal audit function is not disclosed there and so cannot be emphasised, whatever a reader might want.
keywords: appropriately presented or disclosed in the financial statements

options.text: Only the regulatory proceedings, since the other three are matters of accounting and an emphasis of matter deals with uncertainties alone
options.misconception: narrows the paragraph to uncertainty, when the list includes early application of a standard and a catastrophe, neither of which is an uncertainty
options.why: Early application of a new accounting standard is not an uncertainty and neither is a catastrophe that has already happened. Both are on the list because they are fundamental to users' understanding of statements that are correctly prepared.

options.text: The regulatory proceedings, the fire and the early application of the new standard — each is presented or disclosed in the financial statements and each is on the standard's own list of circumstances; the vacancy in internal audit is not in the financial statements at all
options.why: Three of the four sit on the standard's own list of examples. Proceedings out of the ordinary run whose result nobody can yet call are there as exceptional litigation or regulatory action. A significant subsequent event qualifies where it falls after the reporting date and before the report is signed. Early application of a standard ahead of its compulsory year, where that is allowed and the figures move materially, is the third. Each of the three sits inside the notes, and that is what the paragraph needs, because it may refer only to information presented or disclosed by the accounts themselves. The internal audit vacancy is nowhere in them.
keywords: refer only to information presented or disclosed

citation.ref: the four illustrative circumstances the standard sets out for an Emphasis of Matter paragraph, read with para 9 requiring the paragraph to refer only to information presented or disclosed in the financial statements

items.scenario: You are completing the audit of a company that makes industrial chemicals, for the year ended 31 March. Four things sit in your completion file. First, a competition regulator opened proceedings against the company in January that could, on counsel's view, end in a penalty of an amount the company cannot presently estimate; the outcome is genuinely uncertain and note 31 describes the proceedings, the possible range and the uncertainty in full, which you accept. Second, in May, after the balance sheet date and three weeks before you sign, a fire destroyed the company's second-largest plant; the directors have treated it as a non-adjusting event and note 42 sets out the carrying amount lost and the insurance position, which you have tested and accept. Third, the company has applied a new accounting standard a year before it is mandatory, which the standard permits, and the effect on the year's figures is material and is disclosed. Fourth, the company's internal audit function was without a head for eight months of the year; you extended your own procedures and are satisfied, and nothing about it appears in the financial statements. Your opinion will be unmodified, and SA 701 does not apply to this company.

items.stem: Who is right, and why?

options.text: The senior, unless the loss is material, in which case the opinion is qualified for the uncertainty about the insurance recovery
options.misconception: converts a properly accounted uncertainty into a qualification, when the accounting has been accepted
options.why: The recovery has been recognised only to the extent virtually certain and the auditor accepts the treatment, so there is no misstatement to qualify. Materiality decides whether the matter is fundamental to users' understanding, not whether the opinion is modified.

options.text: The partner, but the paragraph must be an other matter paragraph, because the cyclone is an event outside the accounting records
options.misconception: picks the vehicle from where the event happened rather than from whether the matter is presented or disclosed in the financial statements
options.why: An other matter paragraph is for something the accounts do not carry — a matter other than those presented or disclosed by them. This one is disclosed in note 18, so it takes an emphasis of matter paragraph.
keywords: other than those presented or disclosed

options.text: The partner. A disaster on this scale, still telling on the company's financial position, is one of the four the standard names, and the paragraph exists precisely for a matter that is correctly accounted for and disclosed
options.why: Correct accounting is the precondition, not the objection. What an emphasis of matter draws attention to has to be appropriately presented or disclosed already, and to weigh so heavily that a reader could not understand the accounts without it. A major catastrophe still telling on the company's financial position is one of the four situations the standard offers as an example of a paragraph being necessary.

options.text: The senior. Where a matter is recognised and disclosed there is no gap in the financial statements, so there is nothing an additional paragraph can add
options.misconception: treats the paragraph as a remedy for a defect, when it exists only where there is no defect
options.why: A gap in the financial statements would be a misstatement, which calls for a modification and rules an emphasis of matter out altogether. The paragraph is available only where the auditor would not be required to modify the opinion as a result of the matter.
keywords: would not be required to modify the opinion

citation.ref: the four illustrative circumstances the standard sets out for an Emphasis of Matter paragraph, the fourth of them a large-scale disaster still telling on the entity's financial position, read with para 8(a)

items.scenario: A cyclone destroyed a company's coastal warehouse and most of the stock in it two months before the year end. The loss is recognised, the insurance recovery is recognised only to the extent virtually certain, and note 18 describes the event, the assets lost, the recovery expected and the continuing effect on the company's distribution while a replacement is built. You are satisfied with all of it and your opinion will be unmodified. The engagement partner wants an emphasis of matter paragraph. The audit senior objects that since the loss is already recognised in the numbers and fully disclosed, there is by definition nothing left to emphasise.

items.stem: May the report carry both?

options.text: Yes, provided the emphasis of matter paragraph cross-refers to the Key Audit Matters section so that a reader is not misled into thinking there are two matters
options.misconception: solves a presentation problem the standard did not raise, and leaves untouched the proviso that actually forbids the paragraph
options.why: The bar has nothing to do with confusing the reader. It is a condition on including the paragraph at all, and a cross-reference cannot make true what is false — that this matter has not been determined to be a key audit matter.
keywords: a condition on including the paragraph
has not been determined to be a key audit matter

options.text: No, and the matter should be moved out of the Key Audit Matters section into an emphasis of matter paragraph, which speaks to users rather than to the auditor's own workload
options.misconception: reverses the priority, discarding a required key audit matter description in favour of an optional paragraph
options.why: Where SA 701 applies, the use of emphasis of matter paragraphs is not a substitute for a description of the individual key audit matters. A matter determined to be a key audit matter is described in that section, and the emphasis of matter paragraph is what gives way.
keywords: not a substitute for a description of the individual key audit matters

options.text: No. Once SA 701 is in play and this matter has been settled on as a key audit matter, the second condition on an emphasis of matter paragraph fails — so the auditor gives it prominence within the Key Audit Matters section instead, for example by placing it first or by adding to its description
options.why: The second gate closes it. An emphasis of matter paragraph is open to the auditor only while, on an engagement inside SA 701's reach, this matter has not been determined to be a key audit matter and carried into that section of his report. Here it has been. Where a key audit matter is also fundamental to users' understanding, the way to signal that is to set it out more prominently than its neighbours in that section, for instance as the first matter, or to carry additional information in the description of it.
keywords: has not been determined to be a key audit matter

options.text: Yes. The two paragraphs answer different questions — one about the audit and one about the reader — so a matter that is both may properly appear twice
options.misconception: reasons from the difference between the two tests to a conclusion the standard closes with an express proviso
options.why: The tests are indeed different, which is why a matter can be one without being the other. But the standard resolves the overlap itself with a proviso, and the proviso bars the emphasis of matter paragraph once the matter has been determined to be a key audit matter.
keywords: bars the emphasis of matter paragraph

citation.ref: para 8(b) barring an Emphasis of Matter paragraph where SA 701 applies and the matter has been determined to be a key audit matter, read with the guidance that a key audit matter which is also fundamental to users' understanding may be presented more prominently in the Key Audit Matters section or carry additional information in its description

items.scenario: A listed company discloses in note 9 an uncertainty about the future outcome of a tax proceeding that could cost it a material sum. You have obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence about the disclosure and accept it. SA 701 applies. You communicated the matter to the audit committee and, on your professional judgement, it was one of the matters of most significance in this year's audit — you assigned your most experienced manager to it and it took four weeks. You have determined it to be a key audit matter and described it in the Key Audit Matters section. Your manager now proposes to add an emphasis of matter paragraph as well, pointing to note 9, on the ground that the matter is both significant to the audit and fundamental to a reader.

items.stem: Which paragraph does this call for, and what does it say?

options.text: An emphasis of matter paragraph, since the branch balances are in the financial statements and the reader's attention is being drawn to them
options.misconception: picks the vehicle from where the amounts sit rather than from what the paragraph is actually about
options.why: The branch amounts are in the statements but the matter being communicated is not. What is being said is who audited what, which is about the audit and the auditor's responsibilities. An emphasis of matter paragraph may refer only to information presented or disclosed by the accounts it accompanies.
keywords: the matter being communicated is not
refer only to information presented or disclosed

options.text: An other matter paragraph, but only if the branch auditors give their consent to being named
options.misconception: invents a consent condition and leaves out the two provisos the standard actually imposes
options.why: The standard imposes two conditions and neither is consent. One: the paragraph is not prohibited by law or regulation. Two, on an SA 701 engagement: this particular matter has not been determined to be a key audit matter. Consent from another auditor is nowhere among them.
keywords: not prohibited by law or regulation
not been determined to be a key audit matter

options.text: An other matter paragraph in a separate section headed "Other Matter", naming the branches, the total assets and revenue they account for, that their financial statements were audited by the branch auditors whose reports have been furnished to you, and that, for the amounts and disclosures those branches contribute, your opinion rests only on what those auditors reported
options.why: The division of responsibility between the principal auditor and the branch auditors is not a matter presented or disclosed in the financial statements. It is relevant to users' understanding of the audit and of the auditor's responsibilities, which is what an other matter paragraph is for, and it goes in a separate section with the heading "Other Matter". ICAI's illustration of that paragraph names the branches, gives the total assets and revenue, records that the reports have been furnished, and states that the opinion so far as it relates to those amounts and disclosures is based solely on the branch auditors' reports.
keywords: not a matter presented or disclosed in the financial statements
based solely on the branch auditors' reports

options.text: Neither. Reliance on branch auditors is dealt with under the reporting section for other legal and regulatory requirements, so no paragraph under SA 706 arises
options.misconception: assumes a statutory statement about branch returns displaces the standard's own paragraph, when the two co-exist and answer to different readers
options.why: The Companies Act separately asks the auditor to state whether proper returns adequate for his audit were received from branches not visited by him and how he dealt with a branch auditor's report. That statutory statement does not remove the auditor's judgement under SA 706 that users need to know his opinion on those amounts rests solely on another firm's work.
keywords: separately asks the auditor to state
does not remove the auditor's judgement

citation.ref: para 10 on the Other Matter paragraph and its two provisos, with the requirement to include it in a separate section under the heading "Other Matter", read with the illustration of an Other Matter paragraph on branch financial statements audited by branch auditors in Ch. Reporting

items.scenario: A company's standalone financial statements include the returns of five branches whose financial statements were audited by other chartered accountants. Those branches account for a large part of the company's total assets and revenue, their reports have been furnished to you, and you have dealt with them in preparing your report. Your opinion is unmodified. You want the reader to know how far your own work went. SA 701 applies to this company and you have not determined the branch position to be a key audit matter, and nothing in any law or regulation prevents you saying so.

items.stem: What does SA 706 (Revised) allow?

options.text: An emphasis of matter paragraph instead, since the emphasis of matter route is not subject to the prohibition proviso
options.misconception: swaps one paragraph for the other to escape a proviso, when the two are chosen by subject matter and not by convenience
options.why: The choice between them is decided by whether the matter is presented or disclosed in the financial statements. This one is not, so an emphasis of matter paragraph is unavailable to the auditor: it may refer only to information presented or disclosed by the accounts, and there is none here.
keywords: presented or disclosed in the financial statements
refer only to information presented or disclosed

options.text: No other matter paragraph. The paragraph is available only where communicating the matter is not prohibited by law or regulation, and that proviso has no equivalent on the emphasis of matter side
options.why: The other matter paragraph carries two provisos and the first is that this is not prohibited by law or regulation. Where a statute forbids the auditor from publishing the information, the condition fails and the paragraph cannot be included however relevant the auditor thinks it is. The emphasis of matter paragraph carries no such proviso, because by definition it repeats only what the financial statements already say.
keywords: not prohibited by law or regulation

options.text: An other matter paragraph, because relevance to users' understanding of the audit is the test and the auditor has applied it
options.misconception: applies the subject-matter test and stops there, missing the two conditions that sit on top of it
options.why: What the paragraph is about is relevance — to how a reader understands the audit, to what the auditor was answerable for, or to the report itself. On top of that the standard attaches conditions, and failing one of them ends the matter whatever the auditor's judgement on relevance.

options.text: A modified opinion, since the auditor is prevented by law from telling the reader something material about his audit
options.misconception: turns a restriction on what may be published into a limitation on the audit itself
options.why: Nothing has limited the audit. The auditor obtained the evidence and reached his conclusion; what is restricted is publication of one piece of information. A modification requires a material misstatement or an inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence, and neither is present.
keywords: inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence

citation.ref: para 10 on the Other Matter paragraph and the proviso that its inclusion is not prohibited by law or regulation, read with para 9 requiring an Emphasis of Matter paragraph to refer only to information presented or disclosed in the financial statements

items.scenario: You are the auditor of an entity in a regulated sector. During the audit you learn something about the entity's dealings with its regulator that you consider genuinely relevant to a reader's understanding of the scope of your audit. It is not presented or disclosed in the financial statements. The sectoral statute contains a provision that forbids an auditor from publishing information of that description in any report. Your view is that a reader who does not know it will misjudge how far your work reached.

items.stem: How do the four divide?

options.text: The pending appeal and the incomplete note both take an emphasis of matter paragraph, since both concern matters disclosed in the financial statements; the other two take an other matter paragraph
options.misconception: applies the subject-matter test alone and skips the first proviso, which asks whether the matter forces a modification
options.why: Being disclosed is necessary but not sufficient. The paragraph is available only where the auditor would not be required to modify the opinion as a result of the matter, and a note the auditor considers materially incomplete, which management will not correct, is a material misstatement.

options.text: The pending appeal takes an emphasis of matter paragraph; the predecessor auditor and the restriction on use both take an other matter paragraph; and the incomplete related party note takes none of them, because it requires a modification of the opinion
options.why: The dividing line is the subject matter. An emphasis of matter refers to a matter presented or disclosed in the financial statements; an other matter refers to a matter outside them that is relevant to users' understanding of the audit, of what the auditor was answerable for, or of the report he signs. Who audited last year and how the report may be used are both about the audit and the report. And an emphasis of matter paragraph is available only where the auditor would not be required to modify the opinion as a result of the matter, which an uncorrected material misstatement rules out.
keywords: The dividing line is the subject matter
relevant to users' understanding of the audit
would not be required to modify the opinion

options.text: All four take an other matter paragraph, since none of them changes the opinion and the other matter paragraph is the general purpose vehicle for additional communication
options.misconception: treats one of the two paragraphs as a catch-all, and assumes an uncorrected misstatement leaves the opinion alone
options.why: They are not interchangeable and neither is general purpose; each is defined by whether the matter is presented or disclosed in the financial statements. And the incomplete related party note does change the opinion, because a material misstatement management will not correct requires a modification.

options.text: The predecessor auditor is dealt with under SA 710 and needs no paragraph; the restriction on use goes in an emphasis of matter paragraph; the appeal takes an other matter paragraph
options.misconception: reverses the two paragraphs and treats a matter outside the financial statements as one that may be emphasised
options.why: A restriction on the use of the report is not in the financial statements, so it cannot be emphasised — the paragraph shall refer only to information presented or disclosed in them. The appeal is in note 12 and so cannot take an other matter paragraph, which is for matters other than those presented or disclosed.
keywords: refer only to information presented or disclosed
other than those presented or disclosed

citation.ref: para 8 and para 10 on the subject matter of the two paragraphs and their provisos, read with para 9 requiring an Emphasis of Matter paragraph to refer only to information presented or disclosed in the financial statements

items.scenario: Two trainees are preparing a report and have four matters to place. The company's disclosure of a pending appeal, which is in note 12 and which the auditor accepts. The fact that the prior year's financial statements were audited by another firm, which is nowhere in the financial statements. A restriction the auditor wishes to record on the use of his report, which is also nowhere in the financial statements. And a note on a related party transaction that the auditor considers materially incomplete and which management will not expand.

items.stem: How should it be reported?

options.text: In an other matter paragraph, since the auditor is commenting on the significance of the event rather than on its accounting
options.misconception: chooses the paragraph by what the auditor is doing rather than by whether the matter is in the financial statements
options.why: An other matter paragraph carries what the accounts leave out — a matter other than those presented or disclosed by them. This one is disclosed in note 40, so the emphasis of matter paragraph is the right vehicle whatever the auditor's purpose in raising it.
keywords: other than those presented or disclosed

options.text: In the Key Audit Matters section, because a matter this important to a reader must have been of most significance in the audit whether or not it took long
options.misconception: reads significance to the audit off importance to the reader, when the two tests are separate and can diverge
options.why: The label goes on a matter the auditor himself judges to have been of most significance in the audit, picked out of what he had already communicated to those charged with governance. An event that was verified in a day by reading one agreement did not require significant auditor attention, however large it is.
keywords: of most significance in the audit
did not require significant auditor attention

options.text: Nowhere in the report. The event is disclosed in note 40 and the auditor has accepted the disclosure, so the report has nothing left to add
options.misconception: assumes adequate disclosure exhausts the report, which would leave the emphasis of matter paragraph with no purpose at all
options.why: Adequate disclosure is the condition for an emphasis of matter paragraph, not a reason against one. The paragraph exists to draw users' attention to a matter that is appropriately presented or disclosed and is of such importance that it is fundamental to their understanding.
keywords: the condition for an emphasis of matter paragraph

options.text: In an emphasis of matter paragraph. A matter may be fundamental to users' understanding of the financial statements without having required significant auditor attention, and a matter not determined to be a key audit matter for that reason is exactly what the emphasis of matter paragraph is for
options.why: The two tests measure different things. A key audit matter is one that was of most significance in the audit — it is about what required significant auditor attention. An emphasis of matter is about a matter appropriately presented or disclosed that is fundamental to users' understanding of the financial statements. A subsequent event of this size is the standard's own example of a matter that can be the second without being the first.

citation.ref: the relationship between Emphasis of Matter paragraphs and key audit matters — that a matter not determined to be a key audit matter because it did not require significant auditor attention may nonetheless be fundamental to users' understanding and be included in an Emphasis of Matter paragraph — read with para 8(a) and para 8(b)

items.scenario: A listed company to which SA 701 applies signed an agreement in April, after the balance sheet date and before the auditor's report, to sell the division that produces two-thirds of its revenue. The directors treat it as a non-adjusting event and disclose it in note 40, which sets out the terms and the expected effect. The auditor's work on it was straightforward: he read the agreement, checked the disclosure against it and was satisfied within a day. It did not require significant auditor attention and he has not determined it to be a key audit matter. He is nonetheless of the view that a reader who missed note 40 would misunderstand the company entirely.

items.stem: What is wrong with the proposal, and what should he do instead?

options.text: He should remove the loan from the Key Audit Matters section so that the emphasis of matter paragraph becomes available, since that paragraph speaks more directly to a reader
options.misconception: engineers the determination backwards from the paragraph he wants, when the determination is made on significance to the audit
options.why: Whether a matter is a key audit matter is a judgement about what was of most significance in the audit, made from the matters communicated with those charged with governance. It is not adjusted to unlock a reporting paragraph, and dropping a genuine key audit matter would leave the section incomplete.
keywords: of most significance in the audit

options.text: He should add an other matter paragraph rather than an emphasis of matter paragraph, since the restriction applies only to the latter
options.misconception: escapes one paragraph's proviso by choosing the other, ignoring that the same key audit matter proviso sits on both
options.why: Both paragraphs carry the key audit matter proviso. An other matter paragraph goes in only if, on an SA 701 engagement, nobody has settled on this matter as a key audit matter. And the recoverability of the loan is disclosed in the financial statements, which puts it outside the other matter paragraph in any event.
keywords: Both paragraphs carry the key audit matter proviso

options.text: Where SA 701 applies, the use of emphasis of matter paragraphs is not a substitute for a description of the individual key audit matters, and a matter determined to be a key audit matter cannot take an emphasis of matter paragraph at all; he should instead present it more prominently within the section, for example as the first matter, or include additional information in its description
options.why: Two rules bite. The emphasis of matter paragraph is barred because, where SA 701 applies, the matter has been determined to be a key audit matter. And the standard says in terms that the use of emphasis of matter paragraphs is not a substitute for a description of individual key audit matters. The way to signal relative importance is to present the matter more prominently than the others in the Key Audit Matters section, for instance as the first matter, or to include additional information in the description of it.
keywords: not a substitute for a description of individual key audit matters

options.text: Nothing is wrong. The section and the paragraph do different jobs, so a matter that is both significant to the audit and fundamental to the reader may properly carry both
options.misconception: treats the two as independent when the standard has expressly made the emphasis of matter paragraph unavailable once a matter is a key audit matter
options.why: The proviso decides it. On an engagement inside SA 701's reach, an emphasis of matter paragraph is open only while this matter has not been determined to be a key audit matter. Here it has been, so the paragraph is not available whatever job it would have done.
keywords: has not been determined to be a key audit matter
